precedence:
ngv-phase-order: The active pack owns phase order. Musicvideo remains Track → optional Lyrics → Init → approved Analysis → optional existing material → story. Use W10 knowledge inside the relevant existing phases; a replacement phase graph requires an explicit decision.
ngv-canon: Map bible roles to NGV canonical writers/artifacts and cumulative exact-byte lineage. Do not create an independent markdown authority. Draft/proposal and approval remain different states; phase edits require explicit rewind.
ngv-greenfield: Musicvideo may be greenfield: propose story or nonnarrative concept from approved audio analysis and optional lyrics. Missing existing story files never block development. Execution prompts cannot silently invent unapproved beats.
ngv-language: App interaction follows explicit app localization or an explicit language request. Generated model prompts remain English with literal dialogue in the declared dialogue language. Preserve user-supplied text as input/provenance; the normal route still precompiles it, never bypasses the prompt engine.
ngv-hybrid: Reusable craft, coverage, structure, review and finishing also apply to imported/live_action/ai_enhanced shots. Generation-only anchors, paid routes and draft renders are conditional on source mode. Retain zero-generation musicvideo/film workflows.
ngv-anchor-modes: Current locked NGV contract supports explicit frame continuation OR verified native video extension. Frame continuation binds the exact predecessor last frame; native extension binds exact approved predecessor video plus executable mode. Never combine mechanisms or substitute a reference image. Source clean-boundary trimming requires a new immutable derived source and exact timestamp/frame lineage.
ngv-provider-evidence: These are dated source claims, not live verified capabilities. Keep original date/confidence/route. Executability comes from enabled providers intersected with actual route support. Never transplant a UI field into an API or enable a provider from this corpus.
ngv-spend: 3.4 counts one batch of four as an iteration; three or four failures on the same axis fail it, one or two odd rolls do not. One failed run permits one steer/first exclusion; two justify the scoped restatement. Preserve remove → change → add, non-growing repair word count, protected successful lines and clean rewrite/channel change after three failed iterations. Paid batches, tests and 10-of-10 lead stress tests require existing budget authorization; no automatic spend.
ngv-style-scope: Preserve source [edit] tags as assembly-only criteria: they never trigger a generation reroll. Other Verify clauses require frame/clip evidence under their actual applicability; status remains not_observed without it. Selected style controls compile according to project technique A/B/C only where deliberately steered.
ngv-performance-audio: Musicvideo master audio is the original track. Referenced segments can drive performance/lip sync without becoming replacement soundtrack. Singing, spoken dialogue, VO, ambience and score are separate roles with explicit mouth ownership; keep scope of music-bleed exception.
ngv-documentary: For actual documentary, paper edit selects attributed, consented source transcript ranges; no invented witness quote or synthetic footage passed off as evidence. Authored or reenacted interviews are a separately declared synthetic mode, preserving source/disclosure provenance.
ngv-abi-and-pins: Use versioned resources/new extension artifacts under existing registration and loader. Do not add stored fields to compatible public V1 value types. Existing projects retain pinned pack/profile/library versions; migration is explicit and transactional.
ngv-style-risk: A deliberate style may accept a named aesthetic imperfection; it does not excuse wrong identity, anatomy, unapproved canon changes or provenance gaps. Distinguish intentional camera following from accidental floating camera.
ngv-examples: Keep example and template content available in full, but instantiate only from actual project data and verified route. Never promote example light/weather/plot, prices, IDs or account names into canon.
ngv-legal: Preserve attribution, consent, rights and disclosure procedures and the source date. Do not compile jurisdiction-specific legal conclusions into an automatic green gate. No additional legal research or advice is asserted by this extraction.
ngv-knowledge-scope: Conserve the full archive, but select task/phase/technique sections or required units. Do not load large source files wholesale or a second technique chapter. Shared 12h Lint paragraph is available to B/C without loading A; source registry is loaded when evidence is disputed. Context traces prove actual retrieval.
ngv-readable-overlays: Exact text goes to post by default. Preserve 3.4 renderability section 2 documented exceptions separately: master-plate-locked short text, official H3 quoted-text channel and a dedicated template/motion-design route. Each needs actual route support and observed text stability; no blanket ban and no blanket reliability claim.
ngv-project-technique: Choose and persist one technique per project with the director at the applicable creative intake after approved music analysis; no additional pre-analysis step. Unanswered choices remain explicitly ASSUMED with the menu and rationale. One-off W3 assumed A is a scoped exception, not a global default. Technique changes require an explicit versioned decision and downstream invalidation.
ngv-economy: Agent retains canon, scene/beat/end states, reference jobs and required continuity. Only explicit canon, deliberate look or a failed batch on this take licenses a control on a model-owned axis. Record reason and source in Crew choices; do not serialize all populated IR fields unconditionally. Deterministic source provenance and canonical approval gates still apply.
ngv-agent-measurements: Store named model/harness/skill versions, sample count and unmeasured cells as historical evidence, not a current ranking or success rate. Adapt fixtures to local NGV context. Never infer permission for agent delegation, model switching, spending, approvals or PROPOSAL picks from this source.

records.title: Agent Models: Which Model Runs This Skill Well
records.text:
# Agent Models: Which Model Runs This Skill Well

Tags and confidence labels: legend in sources.md. Read this file when the director asks which model to run a session on, or before skill work is handed to a subagent or a batch run. Everything in the table is first-party measurement [PP 2026-09-18, registry entry in sources.md]: a fresh agent got only the task and the instruction to read SKILL.md first and then what the loading map names; it was judged on the delivery and on the files it actually opened. One to three runs per cell, the last of them on the condensed SKILL.md of 2026-09-18 — a result shows what a model CAN do with this skill, never a rate. Model versions age fast: a row is valid for the named version and for v3.4 of this skill.

## Measured

| GPT-5.6 Sol, medium effort (Codex CLI) | passed, three runs — lint counts within one word | passed, two runs — ONE notation (prose with the quoted line), cause before reaction, the vendor-verbatim lock string, lint count exact | passed, two runs — one grouped question, the full technique menu, a reasoned recommendation; the draft-batch offer in one of the two runs | not measured | ranged reads only: the exact minimal set in one run; in another it opened files by their first hundred lines and saw more |
| GPT-5.6 Terra, medium effort (Codex CLI) | passed, three runs — lint counts within three words | passed on the third run — vendor symbols only, the line written once, the music exclusion as a plain sentence; the first run mixed the two notations until the rule said "never mix" in so many words, the second wrote the spoken line again in ACTION | partial, two runs — one grouped question and a reasoned recommendation; the alternatives of the menu listed only in the second run; no draft-batch offer, defaults not marked `ASSUMED` | not measured | reads wider than the map names (look and reference-protocol files), never a large file whole |

Every other model and version: not measured.

records.title: What follows for sessions and subagents (🟡 derived from single runs)
records.text:
## What follows for sessions and subagents (🟡 derived from single runs)

- **Lead session** — intake, the technique decision, canon questions, reviews, a repair that touches the rules: the strongest model the director has. The intake carries the decisions that are expensive to reverse, and the smaller of two same-family models dropped a decision duty exactly there. The same model followed a rule only once it was spelled out as a concrete do and don't — a skill rule that a mid-tier agent must follow states HOW, not only THAT.
- **Subagent or batch work on a running project** — shot prompts from an approved treatment, slates, lint, risk register: a mid-tier model is sufficient once the bible frame is complete (technique decided in bible section B1, assets registered, canon approved). Hand over: the bible frame, the canon passage, the Shot IDs, and the sentence "read SKILL.md first, then only what its loading map names". The lead session recounts the Lint row and re-reads every returned prompt against the canon (checklist step 5) before delivery.
- **Never delegated:** status moves, approvals and PROPOSAL picks (SKILL rules 12 and 14) — they wait for the director, not for another agent.
- **An unmeasured model or a new version:** before it works unattended, run the cold tests below once — a matter of minutes. Offer this once; the director decides.

records.title: The cold-test protocol
records.text:
## The cold-test protocol

Harness, verbatim: `Follow the skill exactly as an agent would when it is triggered: read SKILL.md first, then only what its loading map and routing tell you to read. Do not generate anything on any platform. Deliver exactly what the skill requires. At the end, list every file and chapter you actually read, in order.` Keep the wording identical across models: a sentence such as "the director cannot answer" switches the agent to the ASSUMED path of the interaction contract and tests something else.

- **Prompt test:** a running-project frame (technique decided, two or three registered @assets, one treatment passage) and "write the video prompt for shot X as a complete delivery". Passed when the agent read the runbook, the project's technique chapter, renderability §2–3 and the platform's section — no large file whole, no second technique chapter — and delivered a Render Slate with a Lint row that survives a recount, Crew choices in two halves, a receipt state, a risk register, and cause before reaction in the beats.
- **Dialogue test:** the same frame with technique B decided, two characters and one spoken line in the treatment. Passed when the AUDIO block uses ONE notation (video-prompting 12b), the music exclusion is a plain sentence, the speech count lock is present and the line is written once.
- **Intake test:** a rough idea with format, look and video model named, and "get me started". Passed when the agent read W1, the genre baseline and story-structures ch. 23a, and answered with ONE grouped question that holds the story-gate gaps and the technique menu — three entries, a recommendation with its reason, the draft-batch offer — with defaults marked ASSUMED and bible section B1 named as the place the decision is kept.
- Check the files opened against the harness's own log where it keeps one, and count the lint yourself: a self-reported reading list and a claimed word count are claims, not measurements.

records.title: Director Recipes: Combined Style Packages (Appendix)
records.text:
# Director Recipes: Combined Style Packages (Appendix)

**Contents — read only the part the routing row names:** preamble (packages, cap, Verify-line and `[edit]` rule) · selection index (brief signal → shortlist → constraint filter) + recipe roster · director recipes (one `###` heading each — read only the one chosen) · DoP signatures · harmony map. A recipe's camera, lens, light and colour values are look controls the project steers deliberately (SKILL rule 7), never per-prompt boilerplate.

Optional starting points, NOT a replacement for film-craft.md — each recipe combines composition, camera, editing, light, color, and timing into one coherent package a project can adopt and adapt. Tags and confidence labels: legend in sources.md. Legally these are aesthetic lineages ("References in spirit, fully original execution" — the established formula, platforms-models ch. 13b); never reproduce protected characters, titles-as-content, or scenes. Offer recipes when the user wants a fast style decision. Package cap (the only cap in this file): ONE director recipe (the *structure package* — not the story container of ch. 23) + at most ONE DoP signature = two packages max, one dominant. Never two director recipes side by side — a user naming two directors is routed to synthesis (index step 6: one base, deviations from the other). Villeneuve + Deakins counts as ONE package (Villeneuve embeds the Deakins grammar, see its recipe). Recipe Editing lines describe the NLE assembly; the in-take rules (renderability §5 camera & cut rules, production-pipeline ch. 7 dialogue locks) apply INSIDE every generation regardless of recipe — a recipe may change what you cut between, never what one take is allowed to do.

Format per recipe: Feels like → Composition · Camera · Editing · Light · Color · Timing · Sound cue · Best for · Verify. The **Verify line is the reroll gate**: binary checks to run against generated stills/takes before accepting a result as on-style — a shot that fails its Verify checks is off-recipe even if it looks good. Checks on cut order, VO, score, cross-cutting or transitions are ASSEMBLY checks — tagged `[edit]`; they run at the NLE stage (W9 close) and never gate a reroll. Every Verify line keeps at least three take-level checks. Sound cue = score/needle-drop direction for post (SKILL rule 10); only diegetic sound enters a prompt.

records.title: Selection index: brief → recipe
records.text:
## Selection index: brief → recipe

Entry paths, in priority order:

1. **Genre named or evident** → `genre-baselines.md` carries the per-genre recipe shortlist; come back here for the full package + Verify line.
2. **Director/DoP named and listed** → use that recipe directly.
3. **Director/DoP named but NOT listed** → check the alias table below first; otherwise map to the nearest package on the eight dimensions and say so ("closest package here: X") — never silently substitute.
4. **Mood/feeling given** → mood table below; offer max 2 candidates with their "Feels like" line, the user picks.
5. **Brief too vague to map** → micro-interview, max 3 questions, grouped into the single intake message (SKILL Workflow 1): one-word feeling? · fast or slow? · real or stylized? — then mood table + constraint filter, offer 2; unanswered → ship with the recipe marked `ASSUMED`. Never dump the recipe list on the user.
6. **No single recipe fits** ("something between X and Y") → synthesis: pick ONE base recipe, negotiate deviations dimension by dimension (the eight dimensions are the interview agenda), keep the base's Verify checks where undeviated (cap: preamble). Two directors named outright ("Greengrass + Kurosawa") is this case too: one is the base, the other supplies deviations — never two full recipes.
7. **Always before recommending:** run the constraint filter, then pick the DoP pairing from the harmony map (documented partnership first). House-signature directors (Kubrick, Tarantino, Fincher, Scorsese, Ridley Scott, Wright, Wachowskis, Gilligan) get NO DoP package — the pairing is "none", the recipe is complete.
8. **After the pick:** the chosen recipe (or synthesis) is carried per the project's technique (SKILL rule 4): its load-bearing look tokens in the Caption Spine STYLE line (12h) / distributed across blocks (ch. 12) / as the opening Master Style Block (style-control §6c); a recipe's camera, lens, light or colour values are deliberate look controls — written only where a beat needs them and listed in `Crew choices`, never as boilerplate in every prompt (SKILL rule 7). Its Verify line joins the QA gate for stills and takes. Record recipe + look tokens in the production bible (ch. 22, section B2). The recipe is the bridge from story dialogue into preproduction — not a mood board.

**Mood → shortlist:**
| Brief signal (feel/tone words) | Candidates |
|---|---|
| epic, vast, monumental, sublime | Villeneuve · Deakins lineage · Nolan (+ Hoytema) |
| dread, slow-burn, oppressive, uncanny | Kubrick · Lynch · Villeneuve (+ Fraser or Young) |
| wonder, warm, family, adventure | Spielberg (+ Kamiński) · Miyazaki · Pixar → pixar-look.md |
| whimsical, deadpan, storybook order | Anderson (+ Storaro only if heightened) |
| raw, real, urgent, "found" | Greengrass · UGC (+ Kamiński for combat) |
| cold, controlled, precise, paranoid | Fincher · Hitchcock (+ Willis or Hoytema) |
| romantic, longing, memory of love | Wong Kar-wai (+ Doyle) · Malick (+ Lubezki) |
| quiet, observational, on the road | Wenders · Ozu |
| spiritual, dreamlike, grief, faith | Tarkovsky (+ Fraser) · Malick · Bergman |
| intimate, face-driven, confessional | Bergman (+ Nykvist) · Ozu (+ Nykvist) |
| kinetic, euphoric, music-driven | Boyle (+ Doyle — keep one counterweight scene) |
| mythic, operatic, standoff | Leone (+ Storaro) |
| pulpy, talky menace, genre homage | Tarantino |
| slow-burn, methodical, corrosive, consequence | Gilligan · Fincher |
| spoof, absurd, silly played straight | ZAZ/Brooks (+ the target genre's own package) |
| witty, verbal, neurotic, urbane | Allen lineage (+ Willis) · Anderson |
| gag-precise, beat-synced, genre-blend comedy | Wright |
| dynamic, elemental, ensemble motion | Kurosawa (+ Kamiński) |
| tender desire, the exchanged gaze | Sciamma (+ Mathon) · Wong Kar-wai |
| unvarnished, precarious, lived-in | Dardenne/Arnold |
| sleek, techno-noir, simulated worlds | Wachowskis/Pope |
| propulsive, seductive, rise-and-fall | Scorsese · Boyle |
| dense, breathable worlds, atmosphere | Ridley Scott · Villeneuve (+ Fraser) |

**Constraint filter (veto BEFORE recommending):**
| Project constraint | Favors | Penalizes |
|---|---|---|
| Low reroll budget / tight deadline | Malick (mosaic of short moments), Boyle (montage), Ozu (locked frontal statics), Gilligan (wordless process montage) | Tarkovsky, Lubezki-style oners — long coherent takes mean extension chains + high reroll cost |
| Complex action, crowds, physics risk | Greengrass, UGC, Lynch — absorb or legitimize artifacts; Kurosawa — telephoto crowd planes + weather cover | Fincher, Kubrick — surgical frames expose every flaw |
| Dialogue-heavy | Ozu (frontal singles sidestep reverse-angle continuity), Tarantino, Bergman | Greengrass — verité dialogue coverage burns takes |
| Film lives on face performance | Bergman + Nykvist — spend the reroll budget here | Willis (buried eyes), heavy-silhouette styles |
| High continuity risk (many locations/outfits/characters) | Malick, Lynch — elliptical/dream logic tolerates jumps | Nolan cross-cutting — parallel lines punish continuity errors |
| Stylized/animated format | Miyazaki, Anderson, Pixar → pixar-look.md | Fraser/Willis deep underexposure — clashes with readable-face warmth |

If the mood pick and a constraint collide, state the trade in one sentence and let the user decide — never silently downgrade the style.

**Alias table — directors covered by combination (no own package; compile from existing ones):**
| Named | Compile as | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Coppola (Godfather register) | Willis signature + Leone opera timing | Power geometry static and frontal; ritual cross-cut against violence (the baptism logic — Hitchcock's cross-cutting grammar) |
| Coppola (Apocalypse Now register) | Storaro signature + Malick's elliptical VO-journey structure | Color as ideology over a sensory drift downriver; war as hallucination |
| Cameron | Spielberg structure + Hoytema signature | Action geography even stricter than Spielberg — every cut preserves the map; steel-blue tech sublime; escalation engineered act by act |
| Jarmusch | Wenders structure + Müller signature + Ozu statics | Drier deadpan, longer holds; hangout, not journey |

NOT reducible to combinations — open candidates, add as own recipes only if a project demands them: Bong Joon-ho (vertical class geometry, tonal whiplash) · Michael Mann (digital nocturne) · claustrophobic-subjectivity paranoia (Polanski-style apartment dread) · Herzog (ecstatic documentary truth). Tell the user the gap instead of faking a mapping.

Recipe roster: Anderson · ZAZ/Brooks · Allen lineage · Wright · Fincher · Deakins lineage · Kubrick · Spielberg · Villeneuve · Ridley Scott · Boyle · Greengrass · Dardenne/Arnold · Kurosawa · Leone · Gilligan · Wong Kar-wai · Sciamma · Nolan · Wachowskis/Pope · Miyazaki · Pixar → pixar-look.md · Tarantino · Scorsese · Hitchcock · Wenders · Tarkovsky · Ozu · Bergman · Malick · Lynch · UGC — DoP signatures: Lubezki · Hoytema · Fraser · Storaro · Willis · Kamiński · Doyle · Müller · Nykvist · Young · Mathon. Read only the heading you need.

records.title: Director recipes (structure packages)
records.text: ## Director recipes (structure packages)

records.title: Wes Anderson (symmetry & deadpan)
records.text:
### Wes Anderson (symmetry & deadpan)
Feels like a storybook diorama with dry wit. Composition: dead-center symmetry, planimetric (flat-on) tableaus, meticulous production design. Camera: locked-off or precise 90° whip pans, lateral tracking like page-turns. Editing: rhythmic, chapter cards, inserts of objects/hands. Light: soft, even, almost shadowless. Color: pastel palettes, one accent per world. Timing: metronomic; deadpan holds after punchlines. Sound: needle-drops, narrated formality. Best for: whimsy, families, melancholy comedy, stylized worlds. Verify: subject dead-center, flanks mirrored? camera exactly frontal, no perspective diagonals? light shadowless? ONE accent color against pastel? deadpan hold after the beat?

records.title: ZAZ / Mel Brooks (parody deadpan)
records.text:
### ZAZ / Mel Brooks (parody deadpan)
Feels like a serious film that has no idea it's ridiculous. The META-recipe: adopt the TARGET genre's package verbatim (cop procedural, disaster movie, western) and play it 100% straight — comedy arises from content against faithful form, never from a winking camera. Composition: the parodied genre's framing, plus gag layering — foreground action earnest, absurdity in background/midground planes. Camera: exactly what the target genre would do; no comedic moves. Editing: straight genre pacing; cutaways deliver punchlines deadpan. Light/Color: the target genre's package, unbroken. Timing: gag density over gag size — next joke before the laugh dies; rule of three, the fourth breaks it. Sound: earnest genre score played straight (the score never laughs). (Monty Python variant: the FORM itself breaks instead — intertitles, animation inserts, abrupt endings; anarchy of format, not of frame.) Best for: spoofs, genre parody, sketch features. (AI note: cheap and robust — reuse an existing recipe wholesale and inject gags as content; background-gag layers are still-friendly; deadpan is written as positive micro-cues inside the beat — "faces flat, mouths still, eyes steady" — SKILL rule 6; the PERFORMANCE block only in technique B.) Verify: would a muted single frame pass as the SERIOUS genre? background gag present but not framed as the subject? no camera move that "knows" the joke? score earnest? [edit] faces dead straight?

records.title: Woody Allen lineage (master-shot talk comedy)
records.text:
### Woody Allen lineage (master-shot talk comedy)
Feels like eavesdropping on smart people failing at life. Composition: warm book-lined interiors and city exteriors as conversation arenas; two-shots over singles; characters allowed to LEAVE frame while the dialogue continues. Camera: long-take masters, walk-and-talk lateral tracking, reframes instead of cuts; almost no coverage. Editing: scenes play whole in one or two setups; cuts between scenes, rarely inside them. Light: warm practical interiors, autumn-city naturalism (the Willis NY period: underexposed amber rooms). Color: amber/brown warmth, muted city palettes. Timing: overlapping neurotic dialogue tempo against calm static frames; the joke lands verbally, the frame stays polite. Sound: jazz/classical needle beds; direct address or essayistic VO legitimate. Best for: intellectual/dialogue comedy, relationship pieces, essayistic city films. (AI note: master-shot discipline = few setups per scene = cheap coverage; but long dialogue takes demand lip-sync quality and multi-beat acting micro-cues — budget there; dialogue continuing OUT of frame is a legitimate lip-sync rescue.) Verify: scene holds in one or two setups? characters permitted out of frame mid-line? warm practical interior light? two-shot preferred over shot/reverse? no cut inside a joke? [edit]

records.title: Edgar Wright (comedy in the cut)
records.text:
### Edgar Wright (comedy in the cut)
Feels like the film itself is telling the jokes. Composition: center-punched frames set up FOR the gag, symmetry as setup, inserts as punchlines. Camera: crash zooms, whip pans, snap push-ins timed to the beat — every move is a gag or a setup. Editing: THE instrument — match cuts, hyper-compressed montage (mundane tasks cut like action scenes), rhythmic repetition with escalation, scene transitions that are jokes. Light/Color: genre-bright saturated pop; pastiche lighting when the scene parodies a genre. Timing: everything ON the beat — needle-drops synced to cuts, gags on the downbeat, rule of three across scenes. Sound: effects as punchlines (every whoosh scored), diegetic music timed to action. Best for: action-comedy, genre-blend comedy, montage humor, music-driven set pieces. (AI note: the comedy lives in POST — generate clean coverage of each beat and build the timing in the edit; crash zooms/whips are cheap prompt moves; the mundane-task-as-action montage is generation-friendly — short independent clips.) Verify: cuts landing on the beat? [edit] at least one transition IS a joke? [edit] inserts fired as punchlines — fast, tight, loud? camera moves motivated by comedy, not coverage? escalating repetition present?

records.title: David Fincher (surgical control)
records.text:
### David Fincher (surgical control)
Feels like being watched by something patient. Composition: geometric, ruled lines, subject boxed by architecture. Camera: the "silent machine" — motivated micro-moves, no handheld tremor, camera height at subject logic. Editing: invisible, information-dense, cuts on cognition. Light: low-key, top-ish soft sources, shadowed eyes, greenish-yellow practicals. Color: desaturated teal/amber/sickly green. Timing: relentless even pulse, no wasted frame. Sound: low ambience beds. Best for: thrillers, procedurals, tech dread. Verify: zero handheld tremor, every move slow + motivated? eyes shadowed by top-ish key? subject boxed by architecture lines? teal/amber/sickly-green grade, no clean whites? every cut lands new information? [edit]

records.title: Roger Deakins lineage (DoP grammar, Mendes class)
records.text:
### Roger Deakins lineage (DoP grammar, Mendes class)
Feels like monumental clarity. Composition: vast negative space, tiny humans in geometry, silhouettes against gradients. Camera: slow disciplined moves, long holds, one idea per shot. Editing: patient, cuts as chapter beats. Light: single motivated source pushed to its limit (fire, window slab, sodium). Color: constrained near-monochrome fields (dust orange, fog gray, night blue). Timing: dread through duration. Sound: bass swells, silence weaponized. Best for: epic sci-fi, war, existential scale. Verify: ONE readable idea per frame? human tiny against geometry or silhouetted against a gradient? single motivated source, no fill from nowhere? near-monochrome color field? shot held long enough to feel duration?

records.title: Stanley Kubrick (one-point dread)
records.text:
### Stanley Kubrick (one-point dread)
Feels like fate has a floor plan. Composition: one-point perspective corridors, ruthless symmetry. Camera: slow dolly/steadicam glides, wide lenses close to faces. Editing: long takes, then brutal cuts; classical music against horror. Light: motivated-but-exaggerated (candles, fluorescents), often flat-wide. Color: era-saturated, single-color rooms as psychology. Timing: glacial escalation. Best for: horror, hubris, institutions. Verify: one-point perspective, vanishing point centered? flanks mirror each other? glide perfectly steady, no wobble? room owned by one dominant color? escalation glacial, no early cut? [edit]

records.title: Steven Spielberg (invisible blockbuster grammar)
records.text:
### Steven Spielberg (invisible blockbuster grammar)
Feels like being told a story by a master who never shows his hands. Composition: depth-staged frames (action on three planes at once), faces framed against wonder or threat. Camera: the "oner" — long takes where BLOCKING creates new framings instead of cuts (actors and camera reposition into fresh compositions); slow push-in on a realizing face (the "Spielberg face"); low angles at child eye-height for awe. Editing: invisible continuity, reaction before reveal — we see the face FIRST, then what it sees (builds anticipation); geography always clear. Light: motivated god-rays, backlit door/silhouette entrances, warm practicals against cool night. Color: naturalistic warmth, amber nostalgia vs. steel threat. Timing: suspense by withholding the full view of the threat (show pieces, delay the whole); sentiment earned through delay, then held. Sound: score carries emotion openly, silence before impact. Best for: adventure, family wonder, awe-and-threat storytelling, anything that must feel effortlessly classical. Verify: three depth planes active? reaction face BEFORE the reveal? [edit] god-rays/backlight motivated by an in-world source? threat shown only in pieces? geography never lost across cuts? [edit]

records.title: Denis Villeneuve (slow monumental dread)
records.text:
### Denis Villeneuve (slow monumental dread)
Feels like standing before something vast that does not care about you. Composition/Light/Color: Deakins lineage above + extreme scale contrast (tiny human vs. megastructure/landscape), brutalist geometry, fog/dust as depth; deep underexposure trusted to hold; one near-monochrome field per sequence (ochre, slate, pale gray) with desaturated humanity inside it. Camera: glacial dolly and crane moves with absolute discipline, long approach shots that let dread accumulate, aerials as chapter punctuation. Editing: very long takes, cuts as slow heartbeats; information released in measured drops. Timing: tension through DURATION and approach, not cutting; the pause before contact is the scene. Sound: sub-bass drones and BRAAM-class hits fused with score, silence as pressure. Best for: sci-fi of scale, first contact, institutional dread, existential thrillers. (Deakins is the embedded signature here — Villeneuve adds the slower macro-rhythm, scale obsession, and sound-design fusion.) Verify: scale contrast extreme — tiny human vs. mass? atmosphere (fog/dust) building depth? one massive motivated source? one near-monochrome field per sequence? tension carried by approach/duration, not cut rate? [edit]

records.title: Ridley Scott (layered atmosphere)
records.text:
### Ridley Scott (layered atmosphere)
Feels like a world so dense you could breathe it. Composition: deep frames layered with foreground obstruction — smoke, rain, fans, grids, silhouettes; monumental establishing shots; figures INSIDE environments, never in front of them. Camera: classical moves through volumetric space, slow reveals of scale, hard cuts to detail. Editing: patient world-building punctuated by violence; parallel tension lines. Light: shafts through smoke as signature (blinds, searchlights, god-rays), backlit atmosphere over clean key, practicals multiplied (candles, monitors, neon). Color: world-defining palette per project (amber candle-gold, steel blue-rain, desert bleach), always atmosphere-thickened. Timing: dread accumulates through environment; setpieces erupt from ambience. Sound: environment as score — rain, hum, machinery, wind chimes. Best for: sci-fi worldbuilding, creature dread, historical epics, any project where the WORLD is the star. (AI note: atmosphere is the free lunch — smoke/rain/backlight are prompt-cheap, hide artifacts, and read as production value; layered foreground occlusion breaks the sterile-AI-frame look; his ad-craft polish makes this the bridge recipe for commercials.) Verify: at least two atmosphere layers between lens and subject? light arriving as visible shafts/backlit volume? establishing monumental, figure inside the world? palette world-defining and held? environment audible?

records.title: Danny Boyle (kinetic euphoria)
records.text:
### Danny Boyle (kinetic euphoria)
Feels like adrenaline with a heartbeat. Composition: canted and wide-angle-close frames, subjects pinned to frame edges, bold graphic crops. Camera: restless energy — snap zooms, whip pans, low wide lenses running WITH characters; digital/available-light textures embraced. Editing: fast rhythmic montage cut to music, freeze-frames with inserted titles/graphics, time-lapse and speed shifts, fantasy inserts crashing into reality. Light: hard saturated practicals (sodium, neon, fluorescent), unashamed mixed color temperatures. Color: hyper-saturated pop palettes — acid greens, oranges, cyans. Timing: sprint-and-drop — euphoric acceleration, then a sudden held beat of stillness or horror; needle-drop as structural device. Sound: driving contemporary tracks fused to cut rhythm. Best for: urban energy, addiction/obsession stories, survival against the clock, montage-driven arcs. Verify: wide-angle-close distortion present? mixed color temperatures hot and saturated? cut rhythm locked to the track? [edit] at least one freeze/speed-shift/insert device? a held still beat after the sprint? [edit]

records.title: Paul Greengrass (chaos verité)
records.text:
### Paul Greengrass (chaos verité)
Feels like being inside the event. Composition: none held for long — found framings, crops, obstruction. Camera: handheld urgency, whip refocus, snap zooms. Editing: fast fragmentary, geography sacrificed for pulse (keep ONE orienting master per beat or the audience truly loses the room). Light: available/practical, unpolished. Color: newsprint desaturation. Timing: accelerando to impact. Best for: action, thrillers, docu-drama. (AI note: this style ABSORBS model artifacts — a legitimate rescue look.) Verify: framing genuinely found — crops, obstruction, late refocus? ONE orienting master per beat present? [edit] light available/unpolished? newsprint desaturation? no move reads choreographed?

records.title: Dardenne / Arnold (social realism)
records.text:
### Dardenne / Arnold (social realism)
Feels like life won't pause for the camera. Composition: tight following framings (the nape-of-the-neck shot), 4:3 or tight ratios boxing the subject, locations as found — no dressing glamour. Camera: handheld that BREATHES with the subject — following through doors, stairwells, streets in long unbroken takes; nothing a person couldn't carry, no crane, no drone. Editing: cuts only when attention shifts; scenes run past comfort into truth; no montage shortcuts. Light: available only — overcast daylight, institutional fluorescents, home practicals. Color: muted unglamorous naturalism, no grade beautification. Timing: real-time pressure; tasks and labor shown at true length; drama erupts mid-ordinary. Sound: location sound only, no score (or one diegetic song carrying everything). Best for: social drama, precarious lives, youth on the margins, moral pressure-cooker stories. (AI note: the anti-gloss is the hard part — models beautify by default: lock the anti-gloss POSITIVELY in the style anchor — "overcast available light, ungraded camera-native colour, unflattering fluorescents, skin as it is" (a repeated "no cinematic lighting" ban attracts it, video-prompting ch. 14 third class) — and lint outputs for accidental glamour; long following takes = plan extension chains.) Verify: camera plausibly human-carried, following not leading? zero beautification — light believable as found? location lived-in, undressed? scene runs past its "point"? [edit] no score present? [edit]

records.title: Akira Kurosawa (motion and weather)
records.text:
### Akira Kurosawa (motion and weather)
Feels like history moving as one body. Composition: telephoto compression stacking crowds and armies into planes, triangular group blocking, frames alive in fore/mid/background at once. Camera: long-lens coverage of uninterrupted action, lateral tracking with runners and riders, static frames traversed by motion. Editing: cut ON movement to hide the cut, axial punch-ins, wipes as chapter turns. Light: hard sun and weather as co-director — rain, wind, dust, fog dramatized to the point of choreography. Color: B&W tonal richness or bold heraldic blocks (banners, costume as battlefield legend). Timing: stillness → eruption; group scenes breathe, battles land in waves. Sound: wind and weather beds, drums, silence before the charge. Best for: ensemble action, war epics, samurai/martial arts, any scene where motion itself is the spectacle. (AI note: weather is prompt-cheap production value AND hides artifacts; telephoto crowd planes tolerate face softness naturally; choreography is written beat-by-beat — who does what in which order and the state each move ends in, never the body mechanics of a move (Division of labour), one main action per shot (SKILL rule 3).) Verify: motion layered in at least two depth planes? weather/element actively moving? telephoto compression — background stacked close? cuts landing ON movement? [edit] group blocking triangular and readable?

records.title: Sergio Leone (opera of faces)
records.text:
### Sergio Leone (opera of faces)
Feels like myth stretched over minutes. Composition: extreme wides ↔ extreme close-ups (eyes), horizon staging. Camera: slow push-ins to duel framings, crane reveals. Editing: elastic time — long waiting, explosive resolution in seconds. Light: hard sun, dust, deep hat shadows. Color: bleached earth tones. Timing: the wait IS the scene; score and cut in lockstep. Best for: westerns, standoffs, revenge arcs. Verify: extreme wide ↔ eye-level extreme close-up alternation? [edit] hard sun, deep hat/face shadows? bleached earth palette? the wait held long before the burst? horizon staged as a line?

records.title: Vince Gilligan (procedural corrosion)
records.text:
### Vince Gilligan (procedural corrosion)
Feels like watching consequence assemble itself, one careful step at a time. Composition: neo-western wides (tiny figures against desert and sky), foreground-object dominance, the signature object-POV (camera inside/under the thing — barrel, safe, shovel, dryer); symmetry when institutions appear. Camera: locked wide masters held long, slow creeping push-ins, God's-eye overheads, time-lapse skies as chapter punctuation. Editing: cryptic cold opens (flash-forward fragments), wordless process montages cut to ironic needle-drops (the HOW is the scene), patient takes broken by sudden violence. Light: hard high-desert sun with deep face shadows, sodium-and-fluorescent interiors, silhouettes in doorways against blown exteriors; chiaroscuro deepens as the moral rot does. Color: character-coded wardrobe as arc state (the palette IS the character sheet), desert ochre against sky cyan, sickly institutional greens. Timing: slow-burn procedure — suspense from watching competence, dread from knowing the cost; long silence, short eruption. Sound: desert wind, amplified diegetic detail (clicks, hums, tools), needle-drops at ironic distance. Best for: slow-burn crime, transformation/corrosion arcs, procedure-as-suspense, neo-western Americana. (AI note: unusually AI-friendly — object-POVs are prompt-cheap distinctiveness with zero continuity cost, and wordless process montages fit generation limits perfectly: short independent clips, no lip-sync; but color-coded wardrobe demands the continuity ledger.) Verify: one object-POV or God's-eye per sequence? figures small against desert/sky wides? process steps wordless, each step readable? wardrobe color matching the character's arc state? hard sun shadows or sickly practicals — never neutral studio light?

records.title: Wong Kar-wai (romantic blur)
records.text:
### Wong Kar-wai (romantic blur)
Feels like memory in a rainy neon city. Composition: frames within frames, mirrors-as-shape, bodies cropped. Camera: handheld intimacy, step-printed smear on motion. Editing: elliptical, repetition as longing, voiceover over time-jumps. Light/Color: → Doyle signature (below). Timing: languid loops, sudden accelerations. Sound: repeated musical motif as memory. Best for: romance, longing, city nocturnes. Verify: frame-within-frame or mirror shape? motion smeared (step-print feel)? neon practicals + wet reflections? red/green/gold saturation? a motif repeating? [edit]

records.title: Céline Sciamma (the exchanged gaze)
records.text:
### Céline Sciamma (the exchanged gaze)
Feels like desire studied until it becomes mutual. Composition: painterly static frames — figures composed like canvases, faces given the time and centrality of landscapes; two people sharing frames as equals; interiors and nature pared to essentials. Camera: calm, frontal, unhurried; movement rare and meaningful (a turn, an approach); we look WITH, never AT. Editing: long takes; patient shot/reverse of gazes held past comfort into intimacy; ellipsis over exposition. Light: → Mathon signature (below). Color: restrained earth-and-sea palettes, one burning accent (a dress, a fire). Timing: slow reciprocity — every look answered; silence carries the negotiation. Sound: diegetic only, until music becomes an EVENT (never wallpaper — when it comes, it means). Best for: love stories, desire and consent arcs, period intimacy, quiet emancipation. (AI note: extremely still-friendly — static painterly frames are the stills-first pipeline's home turf; gaze shot/reverse needs the 180° lock and matched eyelines; music-as-event aligns with the no-generated-music doctrine.) Verify: frame would hold as a painting? gaze exchanged — both sides shot with equal weight? light honest from candle/window/dusk only? one accent color max? music absent until it's an event? [edit]

records.title: Christopher Nolan (engineered time)
records.text:
### Christopher Nolan (engineered time)
Feels like a mechanism assembling. Composition: IMAX-scale clean wides, functional close-ups. Camera: mounted realism, aerial majesty, minimal ornament. Editing: cross-cut timelines converging (the structure IS the suspense), hard sound-bridge transitions. Light: naturalistic, cool. Color: steel blue/gray with warm human pockets. Timing: interleaved accelerando across parallel lines. Best for: heists, time mechanics, large-canvas thrillers. Verify: wides clean and monumental, no ornament moves? light naturalistic and cool? steel blue/gray with warm pockets only where humans are? each cross-cut line legible on its own? [edit] sound bridging the cuts? [edit]

records.title: Wachowskis / Bill Pope (digital baroque)
records.text:
### Wachowskis / Bill Pope (digital baroque)
Feels like reality is a rendering you can bend. Composition: comic-panel decisiveness — poses as icons, low heroic angles, symmetrical confrontations, trench-coat silhouettes in sterile architecture. Camera: time-slice/bullet-time as signature (ultra-slowed moment orbited by the camera), wire-fu verticality, aggressive rack focus. Editing: action cut for choreography legibility (the Hong Kong debt); philosophical dialogue in formal shot/reverse. Light: green-tinted fluorescence for the constructed world vs. warmer truth — world-coding as dramaturgy; hard specular surfaces, rain and glass. Color: the green digital veil, black leather and chrome, desaturated real world. Timing: monumental pause before eruption; the held superhuman moment. Sound: impacts as sub-bass events, silence inside the frozen moment. Best for: cyberpunk, simulated realities, techno-noir action, transcendence arcs. (AI note: time-slice/speed-ramp is a documented model strength (ch. 14: keep the term, write the visible change and its parameters — each value a look control listed in `Crew choices`); world-color-coding is a cheap dramaturgical win; wire-fu: choreography is written beat-by-beat — who does what in which order and the state each move ends in, never the body mechanics of a move (Division of labour), one main action per shot (SKILL rule 3) — plus hero-physics linting.) Verify: worlds color-coded and consistently held? max ONE time-slice moment per sequence, orbit readable? poses iconic — frame works as a comic panel? architecture sterile and specular? choreography legible through the cut? [edit]

records.title: Hayao Miyazaki / Ghibli (animated humanism)
records.text:
### Hayao Miyazaki / Ghibli (animated humanism)
Feels like wind you can trust. Composition: layered nature depth, characters small in living landscapes. Camera: calm pans, few cuts inside beats. Editing: "ma" — deliberate empty beats (riding, resting, weather) between plot beats; they ARE the film's breathing. Light: soft daylight, golden interiors. Color: watercolor greens/blues/creams (style-control §6 vocabulary). Timing: unhurried; action bursts read harder against calm. Best for: family, nature, quiet wonder. Verify: layered nature depth — fore/mid/background all alive? characters small in a living landscape? watercolor greens/blues/creams? "ma" beats present between plot beats? [edit] pans calm? no restless cutting? [edit]

records.title: Pixar house style (→ pixar-look.md)
records.text:
### Pixar house style (→ pixar-look.md)
Covered as its own sourced look bible: pixar-look.md (believability-not-realism, simplexity, saturation dramaturgy, Calahan light, curated lens imperfection).

records.title: Quentin Tarantino (pulp tension)
records.text:
### Quentin Tarantino (pulp tension)
Feels like a conversation that might kill you. Composition: low "trunk shot" angles, table geographies, foot-level inserts. Camera: slow creeping push-ins during dialogue, sudden crash zooms. Editing: chapters, long dialogue takes, violence in abrupt spurts; needle-drop cuts. Light: warm practicals, 70s glow. Color: saturated pulp warmth. Timing: extreme delay before release (the Leone debt). Best for: crime, dialogue-driven tension, genre homage. Verify: low trunk-shot angle or table geography present? slow push-in during dialogue? warm 70s practical glow? violence abrupt and SHORT against long talk? [edit] chapter/needle-drop structure felt? [edit]

records.title: Martin Scorsese (guilty momentum)
records.text:
### Martin Scorsese (guilty momentum)
Feels like being seduced by what will destroy you. Composition: subject pinned in a world too alive — busy frames, mirrors, neon interiors; the slow push-in on a face deciding. Camera: propulsive tracking oners through kitchens and clubs (the camera as insider), whip pans, crash zooms, God's-eye tableaus of aftermath. Editing: VO-driven momentum — freeze-frames, jump cuts, needle-drop hard cuts; pace as moral intoxication, then the long deflating comedown. Light: saturated practicals (bar red, club neon); violence erupts in ordinary flat light. Color: hot reds and ambers against urban grime. Timing: rush → stumble — sequences accelerate on the way up and hollow out on the way down; violence sudden, matter-of-fact, over. Sound: wall-to-wall needle-drops at ironic distance, VO confiding directly. Best for: rise-and-fall arcs, crime seduction, faith-and-guilt stories, unreliable charm. (AI note: the VO-plus-montage spine is generation-friendly — short clips stitched by narration, no lip-sync; the tracking-oner showpiece is the ONE expensive shot: plan it via the blockout path.) Verify: VO or music driving the cut rhythm? [edit] camera moving WITH the world's energy, not observing it? saturated practicals (red/amber) in frame? violence brief and unglamorous in ordinary light? one freeze/jump-cut device present? [edit]

records.title: Alfred Hitchcock (pure suspense grammar)
records.text:
### Alfred Hitchcock (pure suspense grammar)
Feels like knowing too much. Composition: POV triads (look → seen → reaction), significant objects enlarged. Camera: dolly-in on realization, the vertigo shot for inner vertigo, god's-eye at moral distance. Editing: cross-cut bomb-under-the-table, cutaways that withhold. Light: hard noir keys on faces. Color: restrained with symbolic accents. Timing: audience ahead of character, always. Best for: thrillers, paranoia, one-location tension. Verify: look → seen → reaction triad complete? [edit] the significant object enlarged? dolly-in landing exactly on the realization? audience ahead of the character? [edit] hard key modelling the face?

records.title: Wim Wenders (the seeing road)
records.text:
### Wim Wenders (the seeing road)
Feels like travelling with someone who notices everything and hurries nothing. Composition: landscape as co-protagonist — figures small against horizons, signage, gas stations; frames that hold after people leave them. Camera: patient observational pans and drives (through-the-windshield as worldview), lateral tracking past facades. Editing: unhurried, cuts follow attention not plot; scenes allowed to breathe past their "point". Light/Color: → Müller signature (below). Timing: journey rhythm — arrival, looking, moving on; dialogue sparse, listening long. Sound: diegetic radio/jukebox, slide-guitar loneliness. Best for: road movies, urban wandering, quiet redemption stories, documentary-fiction hybrids. Verify: landscape/signage co-starring — frame holds after people leave? light reads available, never studio? Americana saturation or luminous B&W held consistently? lateral tracking or windshield POV present? pacing follows attention, not plot? [edit]

records.title: Andrei Tarkovsky (sculpting in time)
records.text:
### Andrei Tarkovsky (sculpting in time)
Feels like a dream remembering you. Composition: painterly depth, ruins and nature interpenetrating, figures dwarfed by rooms and weather. Camera: very slow drifting takes that reframe meaning within one shot; imperceptible push-ins over minutes. Editing: minimal — the take IS the edit; time pressure inside the shot, not between shots. Light: natural gloom, windows as altars, candle/fire as fragile life. Color: desaturated earth and sepia, shifts to B&W or color as memory states. Elements as recurring matter: water dripping and pooling, wind through grass, fire, milk, mirrors-as-idea. Timing: duration as spiritual instrument — hold until discomfort becomes contemplation. Best for: memory, faith, grief, poetic sci-fi. (AI note: demands long coherent takes — plan extension chains and accept a high reroll budget.) Verify: take long with INTERNAL reframing — meaning shifts inside the shot? an element present (water/wind/fire/mirror)? natural gloom, window as altar? desaturated earth/sepia? push-in imperceptible?

records.title: Yasujirō Ozu (domestic stillness)
records.text:
### Yasujirō Ozu (domestic stillness)
Feels like sitting with a family as seasons change. Composition: tatami-height camera (lens level with a seated adult's eyes), frontal symmetrical interiors, corridors and doorframes as frames, "pillow shots" — cutaways to objects/townscapes as breathing pauses. Camera: locked off, almost never moves; characters address nearly into the lens. Editing: 360°-space cutting in the EDIT (the cut order deliberately ignores the 180° rule — matched frontal singles assembled from any side), rhythmic regularity. Light: even, shadowless domestic daylight. Color: restrained interiors with one recurring red accent. Timing: ellipsis of the dramatic (deaths, weddings happen off-screen), attention on before and after. Best for: family drama, generational change, quiet heartbreak. (AI note: the frontal-singles system conveniently sidesteps reverse-angle continuity problems — but only edit-side: generate each frontal single as its OWN take (one locked camera, one character, eyeline near-lens), and state the eyeline side (left or right of lens) in each single — the one axis fact a one-character locked take needs for the NLE pairing (production-pipeline ch. 7). Never put two singles from opposite sides of the axis into one multishot generation — the 360° assembly happens in the NLE, not inside a take.) Verify: camera at seated eye level, frontal? zero camera movement? dialogue in matched frontal singles, eyeline near-lens? pillow shots between scenes? [edit] the one red accent recurring?

records.title: Ingmar Bergman (the face as landscape)
records.text:
### Ingmar Bergman (the face as landscape)
Feels like being unable to look away from a soul. Composition: faces huge and centered, two faces overlapping in one frame (profile + frontal), stark figure-against-void. Camera: slow creep toward faces, long static holds on monologue. Editing: sparse; scenes as confessions played whole. Light: → Nykvist signature (below) + hard summer-island sun for exteriors. Color: austere — chalk, black, blood red as eruption; or graphic B&W. Timing: silence between lines heavier than lines; dream inserts without warning. Best for: chamber drama, crisis of faith, marriages, illness. (AI note: lives on close-up performance — spend the reroll budget here.) Verify: face huge, centered, fully modelled? two-face overlap composition used somewhere? window-soft key against blackness? chalk/black austerity, red only as eruption? silence held between lines?

records.title: Terrence Malick (whispered creation)
records.text:
### Terrence Malick (whispered creation)
Feels like memory praying. Composition: low sun through grass and hands, figures wading through nature, horizon-worship. Camera: wandering steadicam that circles and brushes past people, wide lenses close to skin, always moving gently. Editing: elliptical mosaic — moments not scenes, cut on emotional association; whispered voiceover stitches time. Light: → Lubezki signature (below). Color: golden wheat, deep green, sky pastel. Timing: drift; narrative dissolved into remembered fragments. Best for: memory pieces, nature-spiritual arcs, love and loss montage. (AI note: montage-of-moments structure fits generation limits unusually well — no long continuity chains.) Verify: magic-hour backlight, sun low and in or brushing frame? camera drifting/circling, never locked? cuts on emotional association, not scene logic? [edit] golden/green/pastel naturalism? whispered VO stitching the fragments? [edit]

records.title: David Lynch (dream logic)
records.text:
### David Lynch (dream logic)
Feels like the familiar turned inside out. Composition: ordinary Americana framed a beat too long and too centered; curtains, corridors, stages. Camera: slow floating dollies into darkness, sudden static wrongness. Editing: scene logic obeys dream association, not causality; inserts of objects charged with menace. Light: pools of light in black voids, flickering practicals, red lamps. Color: saturated red/blue against wood-panel browns. Timing: scenes held past comfort; sound arrives before its source. Sound: room-tone drones, industrial hum, sudden silence — the true horror instrument. Best for: surreal thriller, uncanny small towns, subconscious narratives. (AI note: dream logic legitimizes discontinuity — model inconsistencies can read as intention; still lock the recurring faces.) Verify: ordinary subject framed too centered, held too long? light pooling in black voids? red/blue saturation against browns? sound arriving before its source? [edit] recurring faces still locked despite the dream logic?

records.title: UGC/found-footage (authorless camera)
records.text:
### UGC/found-footage (authorless camera)
Feels like it really happened. The anti-recipe: composition accidental, camera device-logic (phone/bodycam/CCTV — one device per sequence, style-control §6b four-tell rule), editing in-camera cuts or none, light available-only, color device-processed, timing unshaped. Best for: horror, virality, testimony. (AI note: highest artifact tolerance of all styles.) Verify: ONE device logic held for the whole sequence (§6b four tells)? composition genuinely accidental? no grade beyond device processing? timing unshaped — in-camera cuts or none? nothing "cinematic" leaked in (no motivated key light, no smooth dolly)?

records.title: DoP signatures (light/lens packages — combinable with any structure above)
records.text:
## DoP signatures (light/lens packages — combinable with any structure above)

Leaner format: pure image signatures without editing/dramaturgy; mix ONE DoP signature with ONE director recipe (cap: preamble). Deakins lineage is a STRUCTURE recipe (editing and timing included) — chosen as structure it allows no second signature; inside Villeneuve it is the embedded signature.

records.title: Emmanuel Lubezki (natural light, magic hour)
records.text:
### Emmanuel Lubezki (natural light, magic hour)
Natural light only, magic hour as religion; ultra-wide lens close enough to distort the face (distorted intimacy); flowing unbroken steadicam oners, camera as a body among bodies; sun flares hitting the lens as grace notes. Grade: naturalistic, luminous. Pairs with: Malick drift, survival epics, spiritual realism. Verify: light plausible as natural-only? wide lens close enough to distort the face? flare motivated by in-frame sun?

records.title: Hoyte van Hoytema (monumental cool naturalism)
records.text:
### Hoyte van Hoytema (monumental cool naturalism)
Monumental cool naturalism; IMAX-scale sharpness with soft-window softness on faces; restrained palette (slate, sand, sea gray); practical-driven interiors, giant single sources; aerial majesty without gloss. Pairs with: Nolan mechanisms, cold-war textures, sober sci-fi. Verify: faces window-soft inside monumental sharpness? palette slate/sand/sea-gray? one giant source per interior?

records.title: Greig Fraser (texture-first low light)
records.text:
### Greig Fraser (texture-first low light)
Texture-first low-light digital: skin grain, dust, breath visible; underexposure trusted deep into shadow; silhouettes against atmospheric voids; anamorphic softness with brutal contrast pockets. Grade: monochromatic warmth or bone-dry desaturation. Pairs with: Villeneuve scale, noir superhero, candlelit intrigue. Verify: shadows deep but texture alive (grain/dust/breath)? silhouettes against atmosphere? contrast pockets brutal, rest soft?

records.title: Vittorio Storaro (color as ideology)
records.text:
### Vittorio Storaro (color as ideology)
Color as ideology: each act OWNS a hue (red passion, blue reason, gold decadence); painterly artificial light unashamed of theatricality; symmetrical torch-and-lantern compositions; moving light DURING the shot as dramaturgy. Pairs with: opera-scale drama, psychedelic war, myth. Verify: the act's OWNED hue dominating? light unashamedly theatrical? light moving DURING a shot somewhere?

records.title: Gordon Willis (the prince of darkness)
records.text:
### Gordon Willis (the prince of darkness)
The prince of darkness: top-light that buries eyes in shadow (moral unreadability); amber-and-black interiors, whole frames underexposed but composed; static formal wides, power geometry. Pairs with: crime dynasties, institutional evil, 70s paranoia. Verify: eyes actually unreadable in shadow? amber-and-black palette? frame underexposed yet shapes still composed?

records.title: Janusz Kamiński (blown backlight through smoke)
records.text:
### Janusz Kamiński (blown backlight through smoke)
Blown backlit highlights through smoke/dust; desaturated silver skin (bleach-bypass feel); handheld combat realism OR godlight sentiment — both extremes, nothing between; hard shafts through windows. Pairs with: Spielberg grammar, war memory, testimony. Verify: highlights blown through smoke/dust? skin desaturated silver? either handheld grit OR godlight — never a middle register?

records.title: Christopher Doyle (handheld color fever)
records.text:
### Christopher Doyle (handheld color fever)
Handheld color fever: saturated neon smear, step-printed motion trails; cramped interiors shot through glass, rain, fabric; available fluorescents mixed hot; frames cropped by architecture. Pairs with: Wong Kar-wai longing, urban fever dreams, romantic disorientation. Verify: neon saturation with motion trails? shot through glass/rain/fabric somewhere? fluorescents mixed hot?

records.title: Robby Müller (available light trusted completely)
records.text:
### Robby Müller (available light trusted completely)
Available light trusted completely: neon, dusk, fluorescents, motel and gas-station practicals as the ONLY sources; Americana color fields (desert ochre, neon red, sky cyan) or luminous silver-gray B&W as a project-level decision; unforced compositions that let landscape and signage speak; camera moves only when a vehicle moves. Grade: naturalistic saturation without gloss. Pairs with: Wenders road patience, Jarmusch-adjacent minimalism, urban nocturnes. Verify: every source visible/diegetic in the world? color fields clean, no gloss grade? frame calm, nothing decorative?

records.title: Sven Nykvist (the face light standard)
records.text:
### Sven Nykvist (the face light standard)
The face light standard: soft window-side modelling, two faces one frame, nothing decorative; Nordic gray exteriors, candle-warm interiors; invisible technique in total service of performance. Pairs with: Bergman chamber work, intimate drama, illness and faith. Verify: face modelled from the window side, soft? nothing decorative in frame? warmth only from candles/interiors?

records.title: Bradford Young (deep soft darkness)
records.text:
### Bradford Young (deep soft darkness)
Deep soft darkness with protected skin tones; underexposed frames that stay tender, not grim; practical pools in black rooms; haze halos around single sources. Grade: warm dark browns, muted jewel accents. Pairs with: quiet sci-fi, intimate histories, night interiors. Verify: darkness soft and warm, skin tones protected (not muddy)? practical pools in black rooms? haze halos around single sources?

records.title: Claire Mathon (dusk and flame)
records.text:
### Claire Mathon (dusk and flame)
Dusk and flame as primary sources: candlelight that actually models, blue-hour sea light, night trusted to real darkness; painterly stillness with digital cleanness (no nostalgic grain); skin luminous across tones; frames lit to hold as portraits. Grade: deep naturalism, velvet blacks, restrained saturation. Pairs with: Sciamma gaze work, period intimacy, sensual realism, night-sea poetry. Verify: source honest (flame/window/dusk) and actually modelling the face? blacks velvet, not crushed? frame holds as a portrait?

records.title: Harmony map: which packages combine
records.text:
## Harmony map: which packages combine

Real-world partnerships are the proof that these pairings work — directors keep their DoPs because structure and image philosophy complete each other. Use the documented pairs as safe defaults, the cross-pairings as informed experiments, and respect the clash list.

**Documented partnerships (safe defaults):**
| Director recipe | DoP signature | Why it harmonizes |
|---|---|---|
| Spielberg | Kamiński | Blown godlight + smoke gives the wonder-and-threat grammar its sentiment and its war-memory grit — both extremes in one toolkit |
| Nolan | Hoytema | Monumental sober naturalism scales to IMAX mechanisms without gloss; cool restraint matches engineered structure |
| Villeneuve | Deakins → Fraser | Deakins built the monumental-clarity phase; Fraser's texture-first underexposure carries the later dust-and-dread scale — both serve duration-dread |
| Wong Kar-wai | Doyle | Step-printed neon smear IS the longing; structure and image are inseparable here — adopt them together or not at all |
| Bergman | Nykvist | The face-as-landscape structure needs the face-light standard; nothing decorative survives the chamber |
| Allen lineage | Willis | The amber NY period — master-shot talk in underexposed warm rooms; comedy that trusts darkness |
| Sciamma | Mathon | The gaze structure needs flame-and-dusk honesty; portrait stillness is shared doctrine |
| Malick | Lubezki | Wandering whisper-montage requires a camera that lives in natural light and moves like breath |
| Wenders | Müller | Available-light Americana trust — the seeing-road structure needs a camera that treats neon and dusk as sufficient |
| Gilligan | (Michael Slovis / BCS lineage) | Hard-sun neo-western wides, object-POV wit, and time-lapse punctuation were built WITH the house camera department — the image grammar is part of the recipe; no full second package |
| Kubrick / Tarantino / Fincher / Scorsese / Ridley Scott / Wright / Wachowskis | (house signatures) | Their image grammar is baked into the director recipe itself — no external DoP package needed; adding one dilutes |

**Recommended cross-pairings (coherent experiments):**
- Hitchcock structure × Willis light — suspense grammar in moral darkness (paranoia thrillers).
- Leone timing × Storaro color — operatic waiting with ideological hues (myth, revenge).
- Boyle kinetics × Doyle fever — double adrenaline for urban delirium; keep ONE counterweight scene or it exhausts.
- Ozu stillness × Nykvist faces — domestic chamber pieces of great tenderness.
- Lynch dream logic × Bradford Young darkness — soft uncanny instead of harsh horror.
- Tarkovsky duration × Fraser texture — modern low-light poetry (grief, faith, slow sci-fi).
- Greengrass verité × Kamiński combat realism — war/action documentary punch.
- Kurosawa motion × Kamiński combat realism — weather-blown war epics with blown-highlight grit.
- Anderson symmetry × Storaro color — heightened storybook theatricality (dose it; two maximalists).

**Clashes (don't combine):**
- Lubezki natural-light flow × Fincher/Kubrick control — improvised light against surgical structure contradicts both.
- Storaro theatricality × Greengrass/UGC verité — ideological color dies in found-footage logic.
- Willis darkness × Miyazaki/Pixar family warmth — buried eyes against readable faces.
- Doyle smear × Nolan mechanism — motion fever blurs the machine's legibility.
- Scott atmosphere layering × Dardenne/Arnold anti-gloss — production value against found truth contradicts both.

records.title: Film Craft: Composition, Camera, Editing, Light, Color, Timing, Dramaturgy
records.text:
# Film Craft: Composition, Camera, Editing, Light, Color, Timing, Dramaturgy

Model-independent film-language knowledge — the DoP/editor/gaffer/script-consultant layer. Use it to advise the user (the director) and to make every technical choice a MOTIVATED choice. Established craft knowledge (film-school canon) — unlabeled house doctrine, ranks as 🟢 (SKILL.md Precedence); tags and confidence labels where present: legend in sources.md. Apply through the generation rules in the other files. Director-style packages: `director-recipes.md`.

records.title: 1. The one meta-rule
records.text:
## 1. The one meta-rule
Every craft choice answers the same question: **what should the audience feel, and where should they look?** Emotion → choice of lens, light, cut, color — never the other way round. When the user states a feeling ("lonely", "threatening", "triumphant"), translate it through the tables below; when the user states a technique, tell them what it will make the audience feel.

records.title: 2. Composition
records.text:
## 2. Composition
| Tool | Effect | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| Rule of thirds | Natural, balanced | Default; subject on a power point, gaze into open space |
| Central/symmetric | Formal, controlled, confrontational or comic | Authority, ritual, deadpan; breaks feel deliberate |
| Leading lines | Steers the eye | Reveals, depth, connecting subject↔goal |
| Frame-in-frame | Isolation, voyeurism, entrapment | Doorways, windows, mirrors-as-shape (not reflections) |
| Negative space | Loneliness, insignificance, dread | Small subject vs. big empty area; horror off-screen space |
| Headroom/lead room | Comfort norms | Break them (crowded headroom, no lead room) for unease |
| Depth layering | Immersion, scale | Always name FG/MG/BG (ties into location plates) |
| High vs. low horizon | Sky = fate/freedom; ground = weight/burden | Establishings, emotional wides |
| Balance/imbalance | Stability vs. tension | Tilt/dutch and asymmetry signal "something is wrong" |
**Aspect ratio is a meaning choice, not a delivery spec:** 2.39:1 = landscape/scope/fate · 1.85/16:9 = neutral human · 4:3/1.19 = portrait pressure, intimacy, past · 9:16 = phone-native presence. Choose per story before production (master strategy: post-audio-legal ch. 17); a mid-film ratio change is a legitimate marked device (memory, constriction).
**Combination logic:** pick ONE dominant compositional idea per shot; a second one only in service of the first. Composition changes across a scene should track the emotional arc (ordered → fragmented as a situation degrades).

records.title: 3. Camera: position, angle, movement, lens
records.text:
## 3. Camera: position, angle, movement, lens
**Height/angle:** eye level = neutral/human · low angle = power, monumentality, threat · high angle = weakness, overview, fate · overhead/top-down = pattern, godview, death · dutch = instability. Child/creature worlds: camera AT the character's eye height turns sets monumental (write the height as a relation — "lens level with the child's eyes"; a specific FOV only as a deliberate look control, ch. 12d).
**Distance is intimacy:** EWS context → WS body language → MS conversation → CU emotion → ECU obsession/detail. Move closer as stakes rise; a scene's tightest framing should land on its emotional peak.
**Movement grammar (motivate every move):**
| Move | Reads as | Motivated by |
|---|---|---|
| Static/locked | Observation, tension, dignity | Letting performance play; dread (what moves inside the frame?) |
| Pan/tilt | Attention shift | Following gaze or subject |
| Dolly in | Rising importance, realization | Emotional intensification (slow) or threat (fast) |
| Dolly out | Abandonment, context reveal, ending | Loss, punchline reveals, closing shots |
| Tracking/lateral | Accompaniment, parallel life | Walk-and-talks, journeys |
| Crane/rise | Overview, transcendence, epilogue | Openings/closings, scale reveals |
| Handheld | Presence, nervousness, documentary truth | Subjectivity, chaos — dose it, don't default |
| Orbit | Inspection, disorientation, iconization | Hero moments, revelations; expensive — earn it |
| Zoom (vs dolly) | Artificial attention, period flavor | 70s look, crash-zoom comedy/doc |
| Crash zoom in / out | Shock, sudden realisation, comic emphasis (in); absurd context reveal, punchline (out) | A discovery or a gag beat — the 70s / Kill Bill register [P59] |
| Snorricam / body mount | Panic, intoxication, dissociation — the head locked, the world lurching | Subjective crisis; the worn-product shot (video-prompting 12e) [P59] |
| Earth zoom-out · infinite zoom · tilt-shift | From one human moment to the whole world · surreal reveal · model-world detachment | Openings, closings, dream and scale devices — cheap in AI, dose them [P59] |
**Lens psychology:** wide = space dominates, distortion near the lens, energy · normal = human truth · tele = compression, surveillance, intimacy-from-distance, isolated subject on creamy BG. Depth of field: deep = the world matters; shallow = only the subject matters. (Degrees per video-prompting ch. 12d — a deliberate look control, never a default; by default the lens is the model's and the psychology is written as words: SKILL rule 7.)

records.title: 4. Editing
records.text:
## 4. Editing
**Cut types & when:**
| Cut | Function |
|---|---|
| Hard cut on action | Invisible continuity — cut mid-movement, the motion hides the seam |
| Match cut (graphic/motion) | Poetic linkage across space/time; scene transitions |
| Cut on look (eyeline) | Question → answer: face looks, next shot shows what they see (Kuleshov: the pairing CREATES the emotion) |
| J-cut (audio leads) | Pulls forward, smooth scene entry — sound of the next scene starts under the current one |
| L-cut (audio trails) | Reaction room — we watch listeners while the speaker continues |
| Jump cut | Time compression, nervous energy, comedy of repetition |
| Smash cut | Violent contrast (loud→silent, calm→chaos); comedy and shock |
| Cutaway/insert | Detail emphasis, tension objects, hiding continuity errors |
| Cross-cutting | Parallel action = suspense engine; alternate locations, tighten intervals toward collision |
| Ellipsis | Skip the unfilmable/boring; the audience's mind bridges (also the AI rescue tool, renderability) |
| Scene transitions | Sound bridge (audio crosses the cut — the workhorse) · match dissolve (time passing, memory) · hard black (chapter weight) · whip/wipe (playful momentum, period flavor) — pick ONE transition language per film |
**Rhythm:** shot length is tempo. Long takes = immersion, dread, dignity; short = urgency, chaos. The classic suspense curve SHORTENS shot lengths toward the climax, then holds one LONG shot at the peak. Cut on motion, breath, or beat; in dialogue, cut on the reaction, not the line end — the listener's face usually carries the scene. **Editing dramaturgy:** every cut must answer a question the previous shot raised, or raise a new one; if neither, the cut (or the shot) is redundant.
🟢 **Murch's Rule of Six (In the Blink of an Eye) — the cut-decision priority ladder:** Emotion (51%) > Story (23%) > Rhythm (10%) > Eye-trace (7%) > Planarity/stage-line (5%) > 3D spatial continuity (4%). Never sacrifice a higher item for a lower one; when forced to choose, spatial continuity is the FIRST thing to give up and emotion the last — "if the emotion is right, the audience tends not to notice lower-order problems." AI corollary: this is the license the whole skill runs on — a take with a minor continuity artifact but the right emotion BEATS a technically clean take that feels wrong; pick takes by the ladder, top down. **Scope:** the ladder ranks only takes that have already passed the hard rejects (slop tell, identity failure — post-audio-legal ch. 19 verdict order); "minor continuity artifact" means a ledger-level detail repaired in the edit (workflows W5), never a rendering tell or a lost identity.

records.title: 5. Light
records.text:
## 5. Light
**Systematics:** key (main source, sets direction) · fill (controls shadow depth) · rim/back (separation, halo). **Key-to-fill ratio is mood:** low contrast/high fill = open, safe, comedic, corporate · high contrast/low fill (chiaroscuro) = drama, secrecy, noir. **High-key** (bright, few shadows): comedy, romance, ads. **Low-key** (dominant shadow): thriller, noir, horror.
**Direction:** front = flat/honest · side = texture, inner conflict (half-lit face) · back = silhouette, mystery, sanctity · top = judgment, interrogation, shadowed eyes · under = wrongness, campfire horror.
**Motivation:** every light needs an in-world source (window, lamp, fire, moon) — unmotivated light reads artificial; stylization may exaggerate a motivated source but not invent sourceless light (Calahan doctrine, pixar-look §4).
**Quality & color:** hard light (small source) = edges, drama, harshness · soft light (big/diffused) = beauty, youth, calm. Warm↔cool contrast on one subject = inner conflict/decision point; the practical-in-frame (visible source) anchors realism and is the single strongest atmosphere tool.
**Time of day as meaning:** golden hour = nostalgia/hope · midday hard sun = exposure, mercilessness · blue hour = melancholy, threshold states · night+practicals = intimacy or danger by ratio.

records.title: 6. Color
records.text:
## 6. Color
**Schemes:** complementary (orange-teal: energetic, commercial) · analogous (harmony, calm) · monochrome+accent (control; the accent color becomes narrative) · triadic (playful, comic-book). **60/30/10** distribution keeps schemes readable.
**Color as arc, not decor:** define per act/sequence a palette temperature AND saturation; shifts must track the story (desaturation with loss; a new color entering with a new force). A recurring "signature color" bound to a character/idea pays off when it transfers (the antagonist's color creeping into the hero's world).
**Meaning is contextual, not absolute:** red = passion/danger/power, blue = distance/calm/sadness, green = nature/poison/uncanny, yellow = warmth/madness, white = innocence/void, black = authority/death — the FILM defines the code by consistent use; establish it early, then exploit it.
**Grade discipline:** one grade concept for the whole film (post-audio-legal ch. 17); scene-level deviations only as marked story beats (flashback, other world).

records.title: 7. Timing & pacing
records.text:
## 7. Timing & pacing
**Scene micro-rhythm:** enter late, leave early — start the scene at the last possible moment, cut before the energy dies. **Beat = smallest unit of change** (a want meets an obstacle, something shifts); a scene without a turn is a cuttable scene.
**Tension mechanics:** suspense = audience knows MORE than the character (show the bomb under the table) · surprise = knows less · dramatic irony sustains whole sequences. Delay is the engine: the cutaway before the door opens, the pause before the answer. **Silence and stillness are beats,** not gaps — the held look after bad news IS the content (the post-flashback processing rule generalizes: after every heavy beat, give 1–2 s of visible processing before new information).
**Payoff economics:** every setup pays off (Chekhov), every payoff was set up; the gap between them is proportional to the payoff's weight.

records.title: 8. Dramaturgy
records.text:
## 8. Dramaturgy
**Macro:** the container is chosen in story-structures ch. 23 (23b three-act, 23e non-submersible units = sequence blocks, 23d short-film); one sequence = one production block.
**Scene level:** every scene has an owner (whose scene is it?), a want, an obstacle, and a turn; write the audience question the scene asks and make the last shot answer or sharpen it.
**Openings:** cold open on motion/question; establish the WORLD-rule of the film in the first 30 s (tone, style, what kind of film promises what kind of ending). **Endings:** the final image is the thesis — plan it first, shoot toward it.
**Blocking & staging (the director's invisible language):** blocking = who stands/moves where; staging = the whole frame's orchestration around it. Working vocabulary: **crosses** (a move across the space = energy shift, re-anchors attention) and **counter-crosses** (opposed movement = conflict made spatial) · **levels** (sitting/standing/elevated = power dynamics without a word) · **foreground shift** (moving a character forward = agency claimed; backward = retreat) · **grounding props & business** (props and small physical tasks ground performances and motivate pauses) · **stillness as statement** (the one who does NOT move owns the scene) · distance between bodies = the relationship's current temperature; who turns their back = the scene's verdict. Blocking also sets TEMPO: movement accelerates a scene, stillness forces the audience to sit in it.
