records.text: ## 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]

records.title: 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]
records.text: **Scope.** Technique A of the SKILL rule-4 menu — chosen per project with the director, never a one-size-fits-all, never tied to a model version: Seedance 2.5 (`t2v` / `omni_reference` / `video_edit` / `video_extension`, on Higgsfield, Cinema Studio, Dreamina, fal, ModelArk) — and Seedance 2.0 with numbered shots in place of timecode beats, because 2.0 does not respond to timestamps [BD-off, 14b version table] — Veo 3.1 with the camera line first, Kling 3.x by the 12g recommendation, MiniMax H3 inside its official field schema (platforms-models ch. 21). It fits the common case: a beat whose content is clear and whose craft the model can carry. The doctrine behind it is SKILL.md "Economy and division of labour"; the shape is also the vendor's own — the official 2.5 guide builds a prompt as asset referencing → one-sentence summary → plot by timestamps or `Shot N` → notes for what stays constant [BD-off].

records.title: 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]
records.text:
**Form — eight elements, in this order, prose, no labels other than the ones printed here; no word ceiling (what belongs: below):**
1. **Title sentence** — one sentence: duration, quality register, genre/register, place. `Create a 10-second stylized 3D animated short inside the dark lamp room of a lighthouse on a rainy night.`
2. **STYLE:** one line, 8–10 short positive tokens: render register, light, material, depth of field, mood, motion register, sound register where it matters. `STYLE: matte rendered materials, soft global illumination, cold window light, wet reflective floorboards, shallow depth of field, hushed mood, slow deliberate motion, room-tone sound.`
3. **Character(s):** one sentence per character, purely visual, the reference token first when a reference exists; closing `Keep <name> visually consistent throughout.` `@cat is a small grey tabby cat with wet clumped fur, a white chest patch, green eyes and a notch in its left ear. Keep the cat visually consistent throughout.`
4. **Location style:** (optional, only with a location reference) one sentence giving the reference exactly one job — `@loc shows the look of the room only` or `@loc is the exact background`.
5. **Camera:** (optional on Seedance and Kling; written in every prompt on Veo 3.1 — per-model placement below) exactly one line, only where continuity across internal cuts or the canon demands it: position, height as a relation, viewing direction, moving or holding still. No focal length, no FOV, no distance in numbers on this line — a deliberately steered lens value lives in the STYLE line or its beat (rule below). `Camera: low, at the height of the cat's shoulders, looking across the floorboards toward the lever; the camera holds still.`
6. **Timecode beats** — 3–6 s per beat, whole seconds, consecutive, without a gap and summing to the duration; ONE main event per beat (a beat may change the shot size). An overfilled window is what produces unrequested cuts or a dropped event, an underfilled one makes the model improvise [BD-off] — so stamps are admissible on a take with internal cuts AND on a take declared ONE continuous shot: a stamp is an event budget, never a cut point (the official 2.5 examples stamp a "single continuous take … no cuts"). Seedance 2.5 knows three timing forms — consecutive ranges, a time point ("at the 5-second mark …"), relative time ("three seconds after …"); the beat timeline uses ONE form, a time point may still mark one critical event or sound inside it, and a high-frequency action is never stamped. On Seedance 2.0 write `Shot 1 / Shot 2 / Shot 3` without stamps (14b). Each beat carries the shot size as a word inside the sentence (the 12d vocabulary), ONE action written as its start state and its end state, an observable action or expression for every character the beat names (a concrete physical detail, never an emotion word — a named character with nothing to do is filled in by the model), and the sound as part of the beat, diegetic; the character's gaze after the action or an uninvolved object held in a half-sentence only where the canon demands it or a run of this take has shown the drift (rule below). Every beat ends in a resting state. `0–4 s, medium-wide: the cat drops from the hatch onto the floorboards, shakes the rain off and looks up at the lamp; the lever stays down; rain drums on the glass.`
7. **"End with …"** — its own paragraph after the last beat: the closing image and, on the last take of a sequence, the fade-out (no fade-out on a take that will be extended — ch. 14b boundary frame). `End with the cat seated and still beneath the lamp, the room warm amber.`
8. **One prohibition sentence** at the very end: `No dialogue, no subtitles, no text, no music. Maintain <one thing> throughout.` — the music clause whenever the take runs with audio on (rule 10).

records.title: 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]
records.text:
**What belongs in the prompt, what does not, and when it is complete (every technique — this replaces a word ceiling).** ByteDance sets no limit and names the fault: "Keep descriptions as concise as possible, avoid redundancy, and avoid semantic conflicts"; "Do not impose a fixed word limit" — compress "repeated style terms, repeated constraints" [BD-off]. The first-party rejects of the over-instructed prompts were prompt faults, not render faults [PP review 2026-09-18]; their eight causes are the checks:
1. **No contradiction inside the prompt** — states, timing, geography and names agree in every paragraph.
2. **Scenic, not technical.** Describe what is seen; a technical term that must stay is written as the term plus its visible result ("Rack focus: the focus shifts smoothly; the trees … become blurred, while the character … gradually becomes clear") [BD-off]; lens, aperture and shutter values only supplement a visible result, they never replace it.
3. **Relations, not measures** (SKILL rule 7) — position and distance relative to stable objects: doors, tables, counters, roads [BD-off].
4. **Acting directions present** — every character a beat names gets an observable action or expression, written as a descriptive sentence.
5. **One timeline** — whole seconds, consecutive, summing to the duration; one main event per beat.
6. **One geography** — the same thing keeps the same name and the same place; spatial relationships go through a reference image first, through words second [BD-off].
7. **Literal wording** — no metaphors, no idioms, no mood adjective standing in for an event; a figurative word pulls the model toward its literal picture.
8. **Working lines are carried forward** — a line that worked in the last approved prompt of this take or sequence stays verbatim; a revision replaces the failing line and drops nothing else.

records.title: 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]
records.text: **Does not belong:** anything on an axis the model owns that is not deliberately steered · a second mention of anything · what an accurate reference already carries ("simply state that it should be referenced and avoid repeatedly describing the scene in detail" [BD-off]) · reasons, explanations, quality words, unrequested constraints · UI settings. **Complete when** it states, each once: what is in the scene and where · what happens in which order and the state each beat ends in · an action for every named character · each reference and its job · the canon facts of this beat · the one camera line where continuity or canon needs it · the sound a beat has · the closing sentence. Stop there.

records.title: 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]
records.text:
**Rules of the spine (each one is a measured failure of the over-instructed block prompts [PP]):**
- **One statement per thing.** Nothing is said again in a second paragraph. There is no POSITIVE LOCKS block; a lock is a sentence inside the beat it protects. Scale and distance (SKILL rule 7) are stated once, as a relation between two things in frame.
- **No numbers in prose by default** beyond the timecodes and the duration: no metres, no body-lengths as a unit, no rates ("at the same pace, no part quicker"). A lens, aperture or colour-temperature value only when the project's look needs exactly it (SKILL rule 7) — once, in the STYLE line or the beat it belongs to, listed in `Crew choices`. Which numerals are fixed terms and not numbers: the Lint paragraph below.
- **No explaining to the reader — the goal and a transition contract are part of the form.** No rules ("Rule for this take"), no reasons, no physics lectures, no dramaturgy comments ("the slowness is the tragedy"), no "must read to the audience as": the model receives the description of a film, not notes to a crew (ch. 24b item 1), and ByteDance keeps "the analysis process, evaluation notes … or reasons for changes" out of the prompt [BD-off]. Admissible, once each: the goal sentence that says what the take is (the title sentence — the vendor's one-sentence summary), and a transition contract — trigger point plus method, and what stays aligned across the cut ("At the 5-second mark, the camera quickly transitions leftward using a left wipe combined with a natural dissolve" [BD-off]; the 12f match-cut lock). 🟡 First-party, unverified: a goal sentence may name the turn the take prepares ("… ends by revealing that …").
- **A reference is one job, positively phrased.** `@cat is …` · `@loc shows the look of the room only` · `@anchor_1A is the exact background and the opening composition`. No `Do not copy …` list for a reference used WHOLE — what it must not deliver follows from the job sentence. Measured: with zero exclusion lines, none of four runs showed reference fighting. A reference used IN PART always names its part positively (`@image2 shows the rendering style only`); a VIDEO or AUDIO reference used in part also names what is not taken, from the first run: `@Video 1 is used for the hand movement only; do not use its characters or scene` [BD-off] — an image reference gets that clause only after a run has copied more than its part (style-control §7 Rule 4, [PP]). The scoping clause belongs to the reference line: it is not a prohibition sentence and does not count against the one negation.
- **Negations: exactly the one closing sentence.** A second negation only after the same fault has appeared in two runs of THIS take, and then as a sentence inside the affected beat (SKILL rule 6). The vendor documents negative control for subtitles and audio only ("Use positive descriptions whenever possible") [BD-off] — the closing sentence stays inside that.
- **Sound is written inside the beat, diegetic.** The platform's audio setting is a project decision in the Render Slate, never prompt text.
- **Nothing on an axis the model owns** — unless the canon says it in so many words, the look needs exactly that control, or a run of this take showed the model doing that one thing differently; then one sentence in the beat it concerns, listed in `Crew choices` (SKILL.md Economy and division of labour).

records.title: 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]
records.text: **Per-model placement.** Seedance 2.5 / Cinema Studio: the order above verbatim; Seedance 2.0: the same order with `Shot N` beats. Veo 3.1: the one camera line is written in every prompt and opens it (Google's cinematography-first formula; with an input image it carries only the move); Kling 3.x: camera-first is a 🟡 recommendation (12g) — a camera line that is written opens the prompt; everything else in the order above; Veo may carry the beats as `[00:00–00:04]` ranges (ch. 21), Kling as plain prose with a motion endpoint. MiniMax H3: the official ch. 21 fields are the container — the beats go into the integrated description with H3's cut-point syntax, the STYLE tokens into its style wording, the one closing sentence at the end of the description; no ch. 12 blocks, no second spine. Medium-emulation looks are usually technique C (Master Style Block + short prose-beat story, style-control §6c); a project may instead carry the medium's tokens on the STYLE line of a Caption Spine — the intake draft takes decide (SKILL rule 4); never both shapes in one prompt.

records.title: 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]
records.text: **Lint before delivery — seven measures, written into the slate's `Lint` row for EVERY video prompt in any technique (SKILL checklist step 5), in this format:** `words n · negations n/1 — prohibition sentences; clauses inside one sentence count once; B: once per governing block; the scoping clause of a partial reference line does not count · numerals outside TC n/0 — each exception a look control named in Crew choices · absolute measures n/0 · double mentions none · contradictions none · beats complete`. `words n` is a count, never a ceiling: it is reported so a revision after a failed run can be held against the one before (SKILL rule 15 — never longer). `contradictions none` = checks 1, 5 and 6 above. `beats complete` = every beat has one main event, its end state and an action for every character it names, and the timeline is consecutive and sums to the duration. A numeral inside a fixed term (3D, an @tag, a shot label such as SHOT 2, a timecode, the take's duration in the title sentence or the FORMAT MODE line, a vendor-verbatim lock string such as "100% matches the reference") is not a number. The closing image — the "End with …" sentence (A, C), the ENDING STATE block (B) — restates the last frame by contract (ch. 14) and is not a double mention. A prompt that fails a measure is repaired before delivery, never delivered with a justification. Repair after a failed run in the rule-15 order (remove → change → add) in the NEXT prompt; the word count never rises (SKILL rule 15).

records.title: 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]
records.text:
**Copy-ready skeleton:**
```
Create a <duration>-second <quality register> <genre/register> short inside <place>.
STYLE: <token>, <token>, <token>, <token>, <token>, <token>, <token>, <token>.
<@ref> is <one visual sentence>. Keep <name> visually consistent throughout.
<@loc> shows the look of <place> only.   |   <@loc> is the exact background.
Camera: <position>, <height as a relation>, looking <direction>; the camera <holds still | moves how>.
0–<t1> s, <shot size>: <one action from start state to end state>; <sound>.
<t1>–<t2> s, <shot size>: …
<t2>–<end> s, <shot size>: …
(relative timing instead of stamps: Three seconds after <event>, <shot size>: <one action from start state to end state>; <sound>.)
End with <closing image>[ and <fade-out> — only on the last take of the sequence].
No dialogue, no subtitles, no text, no music. Maintain <one thing> throughout.
```
Filled instance with slate, `Lint` row and risk entry: worked-example.md §3b (a `t2v` take) and §4 (a `video_extension` round — its title sentence is the boundary state, ch. 14b).

records.title: 12h. The Caption Spine — technique A of the prompting-technique menu (SKILL rule 4) 🟢 house doctrine [PP 2026-09-14]
records.text: **Evidence [PP 2026-09-14, registry entry in sources.md].** Stylized-3D short, ~30 takes over four weeks, Seedance 2.5 in Higgsfield Cinema Studio, 720p, 10 s, `t2v` with 0–2 references. Skill-conformant ch. 12 prompts (1,100–1,300 words, all ● blocks, POSITIVE LOCKS, FOV/Kelvin/distances, a `Do not copy` line per reference): roughly 80 % rejects, with structural rejects — wrong scale, camera morph, event missing or wrong, reference fighting — in every iteration round, typically P01–P04 plus an edit per take. Control on one take: a ~250-word prompt in the shape above, four runs, one new variable each (no references → figure sheet → + location plate as style reference → + one camera line). Four of four runs delivered the same beat structure (medium → insert → return/wide) with cuts at 5.4–5.7 s and 7.8–8.1 s — reproducible at structure level, polish-only variance (roll class, no iteration). Every reference did exactly its one job and changed nothing else, without a single `Do not copy` line. The one camera line made the insert cut return to the same axis — the continuity those block prompts prescribed CAMERA + OPTICS + LOCATION MAP + FIRST FRAME + POSITIVE LOCKS for, and regularly missed. Remaining faults were polish only: a push with the head instead of the flank, a closing wide inventing geography where no anchor was given, one clipping. Contrast diagnosis of the block prompts: scale stated up to six times, camera four times, one prop's damage five times, all of it a third time in POSITIVE LOCKS; 10–30 negations per prompt; numbers in prose; reader-addressed meta sentences; rate instructions; references attached and then told what not to transfer — exactly the "stacked instructions average, not add" fault of SKILL rule 15, produced systematically by the mandatory spine of the same skill. [PP] review 2026-09-18: the rejects were prompt faults, not render faults — the model tried to realise what the prompt said; the eight causes are the checks under "What belongs in the prompt".

records.title: 14. Sequence prompting (the generation unit)
records.text:
## 14. Sequence prompting (the generation unit)
**Doctrine: write shot-first, prompt sequence-first.** The sequence — a take of 1–3 internal shots: ONE shot for a calm single-event beat, 2–3 where pace or coverage needs a cut (production-pipeline ch. 2) — is the generation unit; state chains across takes.

records.title: 14. Sequence prompting (the generation unit)
records.text: **Format precedence (binding):** every delivered Seedance / Cinema Studio prompt is written in the project's technique (SKILL rule 4: A Caption Spine 12h · B block structure ch. 12 · C Master Style Block + story style-control §6c) — the structures quoted in this chapter (fal 9-part note, ByteDance base formula, stage format, edit format) and the Higgsfield prompt-builder scaffold (platforms-models ch. 13b) are SOURCE EVIDENCE for content rules, never alternative delivery shapes; "Drop unused lines" and similar usage notes describe the source, not our output. Mapping into technique A (Caption Spine, 12h): FORMAT → Render Slate settings · REFERENCE MAP / casting mapping → one job sentence per reference (the character and location-style lines) · GLOBAL STYLE → the STYLE line · TIMELINE / Stage N / shot-by-shot action → the timecode beats, shot size as a word inside each · Stage "Initial state" → the first beat's opening state · CAMERA → the one optional camera line, or nothing · AUDIO → a clause inside the beat · Stage "End state" / ENDING STATE → "End with …" · CONSISTENCY anchors / CONSTRAINTS / RULES → the one closing sentence, and a lock sentence inside the beat it protects — never a block. Mapping into technique B (ch. 12 blocks): FORMAT → Render Slate settings, not prompt text · REFERENCE MAP / casting mapping block → ACTIVE REFERENCES · GLOBAL STYLE / "The visuals feature [style]" → distributed per placement rule 1 (LIGHTING, COLOR GRADE, OPTICS, PERFORMANCE) + the STYLE suffix — never a third block · TIMELINE / Stage N / shot-by-shot action / [Subject] performs [action] → ACTION (time-ranged segments) · Stage "Initial state" → FIRST FRAME/BLOCKING · CAMERA / "Use [shot size, angle, movement, cuts]" → OPTICS + CAMERA (+ FORMAT MODE for cuts) · AUDIO → AUDIO · Stage "End state" / ENDING STATE → ENDING STATE · CONSISTENCY anchors / [Maintain Consistency] / CONSTRAINTS → POSITIVE LOCKS. Mapping into technique C: GLOBAL STYLE / "The visuals feature [style]" → the Master Style Block (style-control §6c); the story part maps as technique A's beats. Practitioner formats map the same way: the P58 advanced format GOAL / REFERENCES / CONTINUITY / SCENE / STAGES / LOOK / CAMERA & PERFORMANCE / AUDIO / RULES → GOAL = SCENE CONTEXT · REFERENCES = ACTIVE REFERENCES (grouped per subject) · CONTINUITY + RULES = POSITIVE LOCKS · STAGES ("stage N at ~second X, named, what happens, how framed") = ACTION with time ranges · LOOK = LIGHTING / COLOR GRADE / STYLE; P62's "Seedance structure" (subject + action + environment + style + audio) is the ByteDance base formula above. Only the official fixed schemas of OTHER models (H3, platforms-models ch. 21) replace the project's technique; see 12g.

records.title: 14. Sequence prompting (the generation unit)
records.text:
🟢 **fal 9-part production note:** FORMAT (ratio/duration handled by platform) → REFERENCE MAP (one job per reference) → GLOBAL STYLE → TIMELINE (time-ranged beats) → CAMERA → AUDIO → CONSISTENCY anchors → **ENDING STATE** (explicit final frame description — the next take's start) → CONSTRAINTS. [F] (source pattern — deliver in the project's technique per the precedence line above)
🟢 **State chaining:** every take's prompt begins from the previous ENDING STATE ("continue forward, do not replay"); harvest the final frame as the next start frame — the chain case, the one place a start frame is doctrine (production-pipeline ch. 1); on a route with an extension mode (Seedance 2.5 `video_extension`) the harvested frame is a writing aid for the boundary state only, never a slot input; it becomes the literal start frame solely on a route without extension (SKILL rule 1, ch. 14b). **Boundary-frame source:** harvest from the RAW export (untrimmed .mov, 14b) — the ch. 17 trim is a post step on the assembled cut and is never applied to a take before it is chained or extended. The last frames of a take lie inside the soft zone the trim rule names: if the true last frame is blurred or frozen, harvest the last CLEAN frame instead, write the ENDING STATE for that frame, record its timestamp in the slate `Handoff` row, and for `video_extension` cut the source to that frame before extending (the one trim that precedes generation).
🟢 **Cause before reaction:** contact → movement → sound → reaction as separate ordered actions.
🟢 **Occlusion continuity:** if a subject passes behind something, state that it re-emerges unchanged.
⚠️ 🟡 **Terminal exclusion lists on medium styles [P51]:** each of the 33 medium-emulation prompts ends on ONE "Must not appear" list of 5–15 style words (photorealism, 3D CGI, vector art, 60-fps smoothness …) after 200–500 words of positive medium description, and the media held in the shown Seedance 2.5 results. The two bodies of evidence do not contradict each other — they differ in a second property, so the effect of a style ban is CONDITIONAL: the Hell Grind failure (third class below) was REPETITION ("not a game" a dozen times, scattered through the prompt); the P51 results carry ONE terminal list, never repeated, under a positive description that outweighs it roughly ten to one. What decides is how often the banned word appears and how much positive description stands against it, not the ban as such (🟡 read off the two published result sets; no first-party A/B yet). Settled for the agent: techniques A and B write no style ban and carry the look positively (positive replacement first); technique C writes exactly one — the terminal "MUST NOT APPEAR" list, the delivered shape's one negation (style-control §6c), stated once and never repeated elsewhere in the prompt. SKILL rules 4 and 6 state this from both sides. 🟡 **Length is not adherence [P62]:** an LLM-expanded "highly descriptive" 15-s prompt dropped the boat and the helicopter it asked for and changed the product between shots; the short structured rewrite with a reference attached delivered — the refinement-ratchet mechanism of image-model-logic 24b item 8 observed on video; [P65] names the same curve ("prompt boxes are not linear — more detail helps until it doesn't, then it breaks") and reports one to two generations per scene once the prompt sits at that peak.
🟢 **Negative rule (revised — official docs overruled the earlier strict taxonomy):** negations are established practice in official sources, BOTH kinds: procedural prohibitions ("no cuts, no slow motion, no duplicated props, no speed-ramps") AND content exclusions ("no subtitles, no logos, no music", "NOT plastic", "NO blood") — evidenced in fal prompts with shown results, Runway official examples and Higgsfield's official CS production prompts. ByteDance's own line is narrower: "Use positive descriptions whenever possible. Negative constraints are supported for subtitles and audio control, such as 'no subtitles' and 'no BGM'" [BD-off, 2.5 guide] — on Seedance a negation for subtitles, on-screen text or audio is vendor-backed; every other exclusion is platform and practitioner practice, positive replacement first. Remaining caution where positive-only still holds: (1) **image generators/stills** — negations process unreliably; describe materials positively ("matte, powdery, light-absorbing" instead of "no reflections"); (2) **negated emotion/state descriptions in Seedance 2.0** ("he's not crying" → documented confusion). Motto: **prohibitions and exclusions may be negative; descriptions of appearance and emotion stay positive.** 🟢 **Third class — a style/genre/quality ban is RED when scattered or repeated [H-off, P25]; its one admissible form is technique C's terminal list (⚠️ above):** Higgsfield's own Hell Grind rebuild wrote "not a game, no CGI" a dozen times and got a video-game look — "AI models completely ignore the word not; it sees *game* a dozen times and goes with it". A repeated ban is a positive attractor. Replace every look ban with the wanted lighting, texture and camera grammar ("no cheap effects" → the actual light and material), and state any surviving exclusion ONCE (sole exception: the documented-bleed restatement, 12b). ⚠️ Reconciled with the P24 off-screen device (ch. 12: a kicked door written as "not a limb, not a shadow, not a reflection"): concrete-OBJECT exclusions stated once are that device and stay allowed; style/genre/quality words outside technique C's terminal list, and any repetition, are the red class. **Scope split:** negation-OK for prohibitions/exclusions — proven on Seedance 2.5 (API/Dreamina/Runway), 🟡 for Cinema Studio 4.0 until your own test; the third class — evidenced on Seedance 2.0 inside Cinema Studio (Hell Grind), 🟡 for 2.5 until tested, but treat it as binding either way because the mechanism (repetition = attention) is model-agnostic — for VIDEO prompts; on AR image stills the one-time style-repulsion anchor of style-control §2 / pixar-look §9 remains legitimate (24f). [H-off, F, R-off, BD-off; overrules the P1 generalization]

records.title: Official ByteDance guide additions [BD-off]
records.text:
### Official ByteDance guide additions [BD-off]
🟢 **Base formula (6 elements, 4 lines):** [Subject] performs [action] in [scene]. / The visuals feature [style]. / Use [shot size, angle, movement, cuts]. / Audio includes [dialogue, ambience, SFX, music]. Drop unused lines; generation parameters stay out. (Source pattern — deliver in the project's technique per the precedence line above.)
🟢 **Casting system for many references:** group blocks [Characters]/[Props]/[Scenes]; write every mapping individually ("<Conservator> corresponds to @Image 1. Use only appearance, hairstyle, clothing.") — never a catch-all that leaves the allocation to the model ("@Images 1–4 define four characters respectively"). A range is admissible where it defines ONE thing: several views of one subject ("Images 1-2 are Character 1 and correspond to Audio 1") or one group without individual identity ("@Images 6 to 10 for the rest of the orchestra") [BD-off, shown output]. "Do not interchange their appearances." Declare prop ownership ("belongs only to <X>"). ONE profile per recurring character (the guide's do-not-use line is written only after a non-transfer has occurred in a run — economy doctrine, ch. 12 ACTIVE REFERENCES); **select references per scene** — "Fifty references is a casting pool, not a shopping list."
🟢 **Stage format** (official; matches state chaining): [Generation Goal] → [Stage N: Initial state / Primary event / End state] → [Maintain Consistency]. ONE main change per stage. (Source pattern — deliver in the project's technique per the precedence line above.)
🟢 **Timing patterns:** range (budget) / exact point (one critical beat) / **relative** ("three seconds after he presses the button…"). Ranges consecutive, non-overlapping; three actions in one second don't work. The beat timeline uses one form; a time point may mark one critical event inside it. Density decides the cuts: too much content in a window yields unrequested cuts or a dropped event, too little lets the model improvise; whole seconds, no gaps, never a high-frequency action by timestamp [BD-off, 2.5 guide]. Seedance 2.0 does not respond to timestamps — numbered shots only (14b version table).
🟢 **Edit format:** [Edit Goal] / [Source Video Role: "@Video 1 is the sole editing master"] / [Edit Scope] / [Content to Preserve]. **Subject swaps must inherit the original timeline** (write out every entrance, movement, occlusion, exit with identical timing/path/tempo — the Timeline Inheritance clause) + explicit target count ("keep exactly one X throughout"). **Scope every edit in time explicitly** — whole clip vs. windowed ("Change the man's action from drinking coffee to mopping the floor from 4-6 seconds in Video 1, and leave the rest of the content unchanged" — official example); unscoped edits are the documented cause of mid-clip reversions. Describe the change from A to B. The prompt must carry a trigger word or the task is routed as a plain reference generation: an edit — edit, add, insert, remove, delete, modify, replace, change to; an extension — extend forward, extend backward, continue, continue from [BD-off]. Audio edits as their own instruction. Full 2.5 edit suite (camera-perspective, green-screen, audio-category): ch. 14b.
🟢 **Extension rules:** describe the boundary frame BEFORE the new action. Backward guard: mark materials that belong ONLY to the original clip, or later figures/props appear too early; "connect to the source video" is not enough — write the source's start frame as an explicit end state. Seam repair in the NLE [BD-off, 2.0 FAQ]: trim 6 frames from the end of the earlier segment and 1 frame from the start of the later one; where the story allows, end a segment on a cut and start the next in the new scene.
🟢 **First/last frame & keyframes:** name each anchor separately (combined mention binds neither); both images same ratio or stretch. Multi-keyframes: "use @Image 1 through N as keyframes in this order" + state per image; **separate images beat grid collages**. 3D blockouts: rough = timing/blocking/camera/cut points (map every gray shape by name), fine = re-render with held structure; **remove path lines, axes, camera frustums beforehand — they get rendered.** 3D whitebox is its own reference type: lay out set + camera path before the first render.
🟢 **Emotion formula:** trigger → immediate visible reaction → gradual shift (eyes/brows/mouth/breath/gaze/hand) → settled; 2–4 cues suffice; chain multiple shifts to events. Expressions in descriptive sentences, few idioms [BD-off].
🟢 **Action detail by version [BD-off]:** Seedance 2.5 — "Give priority to general descriptions … Only write specific details for a few memorable actions, and avoid repeating the same actions" (the division of labour, from the vendor). Seedance 2.0 — refine by body part with range, speed and force, prefer slow continuous small movements, write the transition between two actions.
🟢 **Translate camera technique:** keep the term AND write the visible change ("Rack focus: … leaves gradually blur while the face changes from soft to sharp"); dolly zoom/bullet time/speed ramp need defined parameters.
🟢 **Language pattern:** language → regional variety/accent → delivery → speaker → line; "authentic Los Angeles English" beats "English". Restate the language if the model switches. 🟡 Accent guard [P20]: an accent word alone yields caricature — write pace, energy and emotional state into the delivery slot, add "natural, not exaggerated, not a comedy voice", and say how the voice CHANGES on the beat ("when the shock hits, the voice jumps and the words get short"). Dialogue direction reads the same way: the broken apology, the pause, the cut-off, the tone shift as observable behaviour with an explicit end state.
🟢 **Precision limits (official):** timestamps = budgets; edits without frame guarantees; seamless transitions = continuity, not pixel identity; **subtitles, formulas, signage, product specs that must be exact → post-compositing.** Unrequested subtitles cannot be excluded completely [BD-off, 2.0 FAQ]: write the exclusion once, strip text from reference images and videos before attaching them, and where the format allows generate in landscape and crop — subtitles appear markedly less often in landscape than in portrait.

records.title: Aggregator/community confirmations
records.text:
### Aggregator/community confirmations
🟢 Review in separate passes (identity → continuity → timing → camera → audio) — plus the skill's own sixth pass, style (recipe Verify line; production-pipeline ch. 1); **repair in the rule-15 order (remove → change → add) in the NEXT prompt**, not only in post; score adherence before polish. Endings need their own time range; drift in the second half → reduce events + restate the anchor at the failing transition.
🟡 Prompt pack as a constant benchmark: identical brief + references across platforms/models for fair comparisons.

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text: ## 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text: The 2.5 feature set changes the WORKFLOW, not just the specs: control shifts from prose to references, repairs shift from rerolls to edits, and scenes are built by extension. An agent guiding a 2.5 production runs THIS doctrine — a 2.0-era loop (describe everything in text, regenerate on every fault, stitch cold cuts) wastes the model. The prompt shape is the project's technique (SKILL rule 4); in every technique prose is for what happens, references are for what persists. Researched against official sources 2026-08 (ByteDance Seed launch blog, Higgsfield product pages/changelog, official Dreamina prompt-guide templates via [X-ext]).

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text:
🟢 **Mode routing comes first [H-off/X-ext]:** every job picks one of four modes BEFORE any prompt is written — **`t2v`** (new shot from prose + refs) · **`omni_reference`** (new shot with a source video attached as reference: performance re-skins, green-screen relocations; duration settable, source ≥4 s) · **`video_edit`** (scoped fix inside an approved take; duration + ratio locked to source ±0.3 s; on Higgsfield this is the model-selector entry **"Seedance 2.5 Edit"** with the "Edit video" task and the VIDEO TO EDIT source slot [PP]) · **`video_extension`** (forward/backward, 4–30 s per round). The same sentence means different things per mode; two modes silently lock parameters. UI-label map (mode id ↔ Higgsfield label, written in the slate as `id ("UI label")`): platform-ui-workflows §1 mode table.
🟢 **Official ModelArk 2.5 guide items (BytePlus docs, via verified reproduction [BD-off, P40]):** `sd25-pe` is the official prompt-optimizer skill (ask any LLM optimizer "is this per the official 2.5 guide?" — generic optimizers produce headed, categorised prompts where the official examples are screenwriter prose with timestamps and a one-sentence summary); any aspect ratio in **[0.4, 2.5]**; export takes as **.mov** when they feed edits or extensions (continuity); edit calls use `duration = -1` and `ratio = adaptive`; **seamless transition between two videos** and **one-click video** are documented modes; storyboards ≤15 panels, line art, no text on the board; video edits are most stable on inputs up to 20 s with 1–5 reference images (6–8 less stable); timestamps in 1-s units, never for high-frequency actions; no mapping labels inside reference images.
🟢 **Seedance 2.0 → 2.5: what carries over and what does not [BD-off: 2.5 guide "Differences from Seedance 2.0", 2.0 series guide, `sd25-pe`].** Know-how from 2.0 holds on 2.5 unless one of these documented differences says otherwise:

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text:
| Axis | Seedance 2.0 | Seedance 2.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Timing | does not respond to timestamps, only to shot numbers; "support for precise timing … is unstable" | integer-second timestamps: ranges, time points, relative time |
| Take length | ≤ 15 s | ≤ 30 s |
| Subject references | multi-view images not recommended (read as several subjects → twins); headshot + full-body | single-view and multi-view supported for 1–5 subjects; above 5, single views as separate images |
| Action wording | by body part with range, speed and force; slow small movements | general descriptions; detail only for a few memorable actions |
| Quality and constraint words | recommended ("Constraint words are very important") | not added unrequested (`sd25-pe`: no "quality packs, stability packs" or generic negatives) |
| Aspect ratio | six fixed ratios | any ratio in [0.4, 2.5] through the inputs |
| Edit / extension output | — | `.mov` recommended for continuity |

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text:
🟡 **Dreamina-only surfaces, observed Aug 2026 [P29, P30 — Dreamina partner channel]:** (1) **Long video mode** — AI video → model "Dreamina Seedance 2.5" → toggle "Long video" → durations past 30 s up to 3 min, single file (CapCut's variant returns separate clips). Behaviour: NOT continuous — an audible click and visible seam about every 30 s, mild degradation, the model re-paces dialogue on its own (rushes, then pauses; timestamps made it worse), 3-min requests errored for hours, and the 5,000-character prompt cap is hard. Treat it as an internal extension chain with 30-s seams: same boundary discipline as ch. 14b chains, no dialogue-heavy pacing inside it. (2) **Smart Edit** — clip → "Edit", or model Seedance 2.5 → mode "Smart Edit": rectangle/brush/arrow/text/eraser/mark annotations, each "Add to chat" with its instruction, reference images inline; several edits (remove ×2, replace, add) succeeded in ONE submission with reflections and ground patterns held, slight degradation at 720p — but the AUDIO of a removed subject stayed (footsteps): pair every visual removal with an audio-category edit. Dreamina also exposes a reference-weight slider (unverified, [P35]).
🟢 **Music track as timing input [H-off, P48, Seedance 2.0 on Higgsfield]:** "add the music track as an input and have the hero dance in time with its beat" — the track is loaded as an audio reference beside the prompt and every move landed on the beat; a TIMING reference, not generated score (rule 10 holds). Choreography still needs move-by-move language (renderability §3).

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text:
🟢 **Plan the reference set BEFORE the prose [BD-off].** Official capacity: 30 images + 10 video + 10 audio per generation; ByteDance: "a larger volume and wider variety of references can better capture the user's intent." The agent's duty at shot-brief time: walk the shot's element list and give EVERY element that must stay consistent its own reference — characters (4-view sheet, one view a strong expression), wardrobe, key props, location plates, style still, motion clips, voice/audio, clay blockout. **Prose is for what happens; references are for what persists** — an element controlled only by text will drift. Reference-maximal ≠ reference-dump: stability ranges: the 12b budgets [X-ext]; one deliberate reference per element beats a cluttered set [H-off]. Selection stays per-scene (casting pool, ch. 14) — but the POOL is built out maximally as a project asset (production-pipeline ch. 1).
⚠️ 🟡 **Single-view images per subject instead of one sheet [P58, sponsored, ~$2,000 of tests]:** with 30 image slots one practitioner stopped attaching collage sheets on 2.5 and gives ONE subject four face angles plus four body angles as separate single images, declared together as one distinct subject in the casting block ("more context per subject"); products get six single-view angles the same way. Conflicts with the feature-film sheet doctrine (production-pipeline ch. 3, [P24], 🟢, proven on 2.0 with headless sheets); the ByteDance ">5 subjects → single-view images" rule points the same way for cameos. ByteDance settles the scope [BD-off]: on 2.5 single-view AND multi-view inputs are supported for 1–5 subjects; above 5, single views are more stable and several views go into separate images, never one combined image; on 2.0 multi-view images are not recommended at all (headshot + full-body instead). Treat it as a legitimate 2.5 alternative for the 1–3 leads when the slot budget allows: the identity source is still ONE clean face, now spread over several single-view files instead of panels; the ten-of-ten stress test decides between the two formats, not the format itself.

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text: 🟢 **The four reference classes and their default jobs [BD-off]:** `@Image` = identity/appearance · `@Video` = **motion/pacing by default, not identity** — say so explicitly when you mean otherwise · `@Audio` = voice/dialogue/ambience/music via a role line ("@Audio 1 defines <character>'s voice") — voice consistency across scenes is an official capability, and audio refs drive lip-sync performance · **`@Clay Render`** = staging (official ByteDance reference class): a textureless 3D blockout carries "camera movement, pacing, shot-size transitions, subject trajectory, and blocking"; 2.5 derives physically plausible LIGHTING (source direction, colour temperature, shadow projection) from its spatial info on its own — but the lighting JOB is assigned to an image reference's role line, never to the clay render's ("Refer to @Clay Render 1 for camera movement… @Image 2 for character design, scene, materials, lighting, color" is the official pattern; production-pipeline ch. 8 role split). Coarse vs. fine blockout discipline: ch. 14 (strip path lines, axes, camera frustums — they render as content). On Higgsfield, attach the Blender viewport render/recording as a normal reference (Blender plugin, platforms-models ch. 13). **The clay render is also the hard SIZE and staging control for props/creatures** — the video-side answer to image-model-logic ch. 24d.

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text:
🟢 **Voice channel per character — text half always, reference half by surface:** the verbatim voice-conditions block (12b) is the TEXT half and goes into every take where the character speaks. The REFERENCE half is exactly one of, in this order: (1) a saved/cloned platform voice where the surface offers one (post-audio-legal ch. 18); (2) an `@Audio` reference — one compilation of the character's approved generated lines, combined <30 s, uploaded as an AUDIO file, role line "@Audio N defines <character>'s voice — timbre and manner only, do not reuse its words" (the audio-slot form of the ch. 18 P17 harvest); (3) the surface takes video but no audio references: the ch. 18 P17 black-screen MP4 as `@Video`, role line "@Video N carries <character>'s voice only — it is not a motion, pacing or framing reference" (the exclusion is mandatory: @Video defaults to motion). Never attach the same compilation as both @Audio and @Video; never list a voice reference for a character who has no line in the take (12b tag rule).
🟡 **Deriving the text half from a sample [P52]:** upload a real recording of the intended voice to the text LLM and ask for a voice prompt (pitch, timbre, cadence, energy, accent); freeze the result verbatim per 12b. Generated lines from a TTS service can serve as the reference half where the surface takes audio or black-screen video references (post-audio-legal ch. 18) — consent and licence terms of that voice apply (ch. 20).
🟡 **A third `@Audio` job — diegetic playback [P57]:** beside voice and timing input, an attached track can be the sound source INSIDE the scene: `@Audio 1 is the song playing on the car radio — the characters hear it and react`; two listeners nodded to the beat and called the song "fire", a driver sang along to a track that "played through the radio". Pool ceiling 30 s combined; the model also invented a radio-host intro line around the track (12b invented-dialogue risk — lock the spoken text). One class per audio file: never voice and music in one upload [P58].

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text:
🟢 **The edit suite — repair before reroll.** An approved take is never regenerated for a local fault. All official [BD-off], all invoked as prompts (Higgsfield's Video page exposes no mask/annotation editor as of 2026-08-31 — describe the region in words; 🟡 a draw-over tool was sighted in Cinema Studio's Edit → Advanced on 2026-09-01, platform-ui-workflows §1):
- **Region edit:** `[what] + [change] + [effective time range]` — "repaints just that region, no full regeneration, no seed lottery" [H-off]. Always time-scope (ch. 14 edit format).
- **Camera-perspective edit = a B-camera pass on an approved performance:** "Edit @Video 1. Keep the characters, actions, and visual style unchanged. Adjust only the camera movement." + a segmented camera plan per time range (official worked prompt). Coverage tool: production-pipeline ch. 16 rung 2.
- **Green-screen relocation** (runs as `omni_reference` with the source clip attached): moves a performance into a new environment; the model adapts cloth flutter, hair, gait rhythm, and lighting interaction to the new scene.
- **Subject swap:** Timeline Inheritance clause mandatory (ch. 14).
- **Audio-category edits:** dialogue, spoken language, voice, BGM, SFX edit independently ("Remove only the original background music. Keep the character dialogue, lip sync, ambience, and action sound effects").
Constraints [X-ext]: edit source ≤20 s recommended, 1–5 accompanying refs; **an edit bills the source's FULL duration on Higgsfield** — the saving is fewer attempts, not per-run price. Consequence: **draft at the take's planned length (10 s by default); once the beats lock, regenerate the locked prompt as a fresh full-length take at target resolution (never extend the draft — extension is for building length PAST a full take, next paragraph); from then on every fix is an edit.** ⚠️ **Edit-round ceiling — by analogy, no 2.5-specific evidence yet:** treat chained video edits like image edit chains (style-control §2, image-model-logic ch. 24g multi-turn collapse): after 3 edit rounds on one source, stop chaining. Export the best intermediate as .mov (ModelArk item above), register it as the new `@Video 1` source, and continue edits from that file; if the remaining fault is global, regenerate from the original references instead (W8 / production-pipeline ch. 1 review loop). Log each edit round as a Take ID.

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text:
🟢 **Extension chains [BD-off]:** 4–30 s per round, forward or backward; carries main characters, environment, narrative pacing, audio continuity. **Chain ceiling ≈60 s** (30 s source + one 30 s extension) — beyond that, re-anchor a NEW generation from the original references instead of extending an extension (degradation compounds). Boundary-frame contract every round: forward — "the first frame of the extended segment directly continues from the last frame of @Video 1" (the last clean frame — boundary-frame source, ch. 14); backward — write the source's first frame as the extension's explicit END state and declare which materials must not appear early ("then connect to the source video" is the documented failure; ch. 14 extension rules). Restate the continuity list each round. 180 s single-flow is a Dreamina-only beta, not a Higgsfield plan (⚠️ [P58] reported a 180-s option on the Higgsfield surface in Aug 2026 — "six 30-s videos stitched from one 5,000-character prompt" — same mechanism, same verdict: not for held scenes; read the live form). 🟡 **Copy-ready extension wording that held without extra references [P57]:** forward — `Extend @Video 1 forward, directly continued from its last frame, matching the subject's pose, position, background, camera angle, lighting and motion direction. New action: …`; backward — `Extend @Video 1 backward: before the video starts, …` (a 19-s prequel cut cleanly against the source's first 5 s). 🟡 **Video-as-reference continuation drifts geometry [P52]:** "continue from @Video 1" with the clip attached as a reference (omni-style, not an extension) changed a prop's size between clips; extension or last-frame chaining holds geometry better — if omni continuation is used, attach the prop as its own reference.
🟡 **One location per take for narrative intercuts [P28, Seedance 2.0 evidence]:** do not prompt A/B parallel action inside one generation (hero ship ↔ enemy ship); generate one take per location and cut in the NLE — the complexity budget (SKILL rule 3) applied to locations. Montage/commercial takes (next line) are exempt: they may span locations because no parallel action is implied. ⚠️ Scope [H-off, P66]: the rule holds for text-only prompting; a continuous JOURNEY through several locations (street → corridor → kitchen → casino, 30 s) held on 2.5 when a clay render carried the route (production-pipeline ch. 8 protocol c) — parallel intercuts stay one-location-per-take, a travelled route with a blockout does not.
🟡 **Montage ceiling and the missing agent [P38]:** commercials/montages are the exception to the 2–3-shot drama budget — cap at **12–15 cuts per 30-s take** ("so it can focus on each cut"; an LLM's first draft had far more). Name the ACTOR of every action: "onions are chopped" rendered a kitchen with no hands in frame — write "the chef's hands chop". 🟢 **Everything unreferenced goes static — write background life explicitly [P39, P41; H-off, P69]:** with ~9 references the composite held but crowd and sky froze; the vendor's harbour scene had "NPC crowds staring into space" until the prompt forced every background person to be mid-action in every frame — write it ("people moving in the beach bar", "every passer-by mid-stride") or get a ghost town. The same vendor fix for a beat that over-shot (a shoulder bump rendered as a hug): write the physical mechanics — shoulders hit, suitcases swing, momentum carries them half a step past, planted feet turn — "when the collision becomes physics, the romance feels natural" (ch. 14 cause before reaction).
🟡 **Write the boundary state from harvested frames [P22]:** before prompting an extension, frame-harvest the source's first/last frame plus 2–3 keyframes, and let the agent write the continuation FROM those stills — who stands where, what each hand holds, where the light comes from — so positions, hand contact and eyeline are held verbatim ("his hand stays on the side of the washing machine"). A well-anchored extension cut together with its source was reported seamless.

records.title: 14b. Seedance 2.5 production doctrine — references, edit suite, extension chains
records.text:
🟢 **Timestamp control is a documented channel at generation AND edit time [BD-off]:** the three ch. 14 timing forms (range / exact point / relative) hold at edit time too; every timed segment ends on an explicit end state. Still budgets, not frames — "timestamps allocate proportion, not frames" [F]: never demand events inside one second, never plan frame-accurate hits (precision limits, ch. 14).
🟢 **Beats inside a declared single shot — settled by version [BD-off; H-off P47 vs P49 for 2.0]:** Seedance 2.5 takes integer-second stamps inside one continuous take — a stamp is an event budget, never a cut point, and the official examples stamp a "single continuous take … no cuts". What produces unrequested cuts is an overfilled window (ch. 14 timing patterns): give each window one main event, or use relative timing. Seedance 2.0 does not respond to timestamps — numbered shots or relative timing; the two conflicting Higgsfield observations (per-second beats worked / "forcing Seedance to do cuts") are 2.0 behaviour and stay version-dated.

records.title: 15. Style enforcement & reference integration
records.text:
## 15. Style enforcement & reference integration
Fully externalized to **`style-control.md`** (style stack hierarchy, model-specific mechanics for GPT Image 2.5 / Nano Banana Pro / video models — incl. the production-proven 4-section Pixar prompt structure in §2 — 11 animation vocabularies (§6) + footage/era/optics packages (§6b), reference integration protocol, diagnosis). Read that file for ANY stylized-look task and whenever writing prompts that use references.

records.text: # Worked Example: 20-Second Spot, End to End

records.title: Worked Example: 20-Second Spot, End to End
records.text: **Contents — read once end to end on first use; afterwards only the part a pointer names:** §1 canon → shot plan · §1b route receipt · §2 assets · §3 sequence take S1 in technique B (block structure, for comparison) · §3b the same take in technique A (Caption Spine — the technique this project chose) · §3c production take of S1 · §4 sequence take S2, extension round · §5 QA and log.

records.title: Worked Example: 20-Second Spot, End to End
records.text: A compact walkthrough applying the pipeline to a fictional brief — read once to see how the chapters connect; every deliverable below is in the form the rules require (per-prompt checklist steps 1–7, Render Slate, risk register, bible rows). Style: Pixar-adjacent stylized 3D (in a real project the style is picked via the director-recipes selection index — here fixed for brevity). Model path: Nano Banana Pro (figure-anchored anchor plate, sheets) → GPT Image 2.5 (derived empty plate, reverse plate) → Seedance 2.5 on Higgsfield (motion). Project slug: `LIGHTCAT`. Element tags (Higgsfield Elements, verbatim everywhere — tag token rule, video-prompting ch. 12b): `@cat`, `@loc_lamproom`, `@loc_lamproom_rev`, `@prop_lever`, `@anchor_1A`, `@anchor_1B`. On a Dreamina/ModelArk surface the same prompts would carry `@Image 1…n` by upload order. Sequence take S1 is shown in BOTH prompt shapes on the same canon: §3b is the Caption Spine — the technique this example project chose at intake (SKILL rule 4; read this one first) — and §3 is the same take in the block structure, for comparison; the extension round (§4) is in the Caption Spine. Both carry the same Render ID: the technique is a project constant, not a prompt variant.

records.title: 1. Canon → shot plan (SKILL rule 14, production-pipeline ch. 2)
records.text:
## 1. Canon → shot plan (SKILL rule 14, production-pipeline ch. 2)
Canon comes from the director's treatment — never from the agent. Treatment excerpt (the passage every canon-bound claim below is read from): "Sc. 1, night, rain. The keeper's cat slips through the hatch into the dark lamp room, shakes off, rears up and pushes the brass lever with its whole body. The lamp ignites; the cat sits and watches the beam." Canon is silent on where the cat enters from → delivered as `PROPOSAL — not canon` ("hatch at the left wall"), approved by the director before it entered any prompt. Camera height and light direction are craft-fillable (rule 14) — decided by the crew and listed in each slate's `Crew choices` row; the lens, the composition inside the named shot size and the cut timing are left to the model by default (SKILL.md Economy and division of labour), and the `Crew choices` row says so. Intake decision (SKILL rule 4): technique A, Caption Spine — a calm single-event beat with clear canon and a look the anchors carry; no draft takes were needed. Recorded in the bible frame (section B1).
Renderability pass: paw-level object manipulation 🟡 (renderability §2 hands row) → rescue: whole-body push (big motion, no finger-class precision); rescue cut if it fails: lever-only insert + reaction MCU. Both takes contain a cut for coverage; a calm single-event beat would be ONE shot in one take (production-pipeline ch. 2).

records.title: 1. Canon → shot plan (SKILL rule 14, production-pipeline ch. 2)
records.text:

records.title: 3. Sequence take S1 (shots 1A+1B) — technique B, block structure (video-prompting ch. 12/12b/14; style-control §5/§7) — shown for comparison
records.text:
```
SCENE CONTEXT: Night, rain, lamp room of a lighthouse. @cat has just slipped in through the hatch and will push the brass lever to relight the dark lamp above.
ACTIVE REFERENCES: @anchor_1A is the opening composition of SHOT 1 (0.0–4.0 s) and of SHOT 3 (7.0–10.0 s); the take opens already in motion. @anchor_1B is the opening composition of SHOT 2, from the HARD CUT at 4.0 s onward. @cat controls only the cat — small grey tabby, wet clumped fur, white chest patch, green eyes, one notch in the left ear. 100% matches the reference. @loc_lamproom controls only the set. 100% matches the reference. @prop_lever controls only the lever — shape, state: down. 100% matches the reference.
LOCATION MAP: foreground wet floorboards; midground the brass lever on the right wall, the hatch on the left wall; background rain-streaked windows, the dark lamp above centre. Camera in the rear-left corner of the room.
FIRST FRAME/BLOCKING: the cat mid-squeeze through the half-open hatch, body toward frame centre, gaze up at the lamp.
FORMAT MODE: sequential cuts, three shots, 10 s total — Shot 1 0.0–4.0 s, Shot 2 4.0–7.0 s, Shot 3 7.0–10.0 s.
OPTICS: Shots 1 and 3 medium-wide at 63°; Shot 2 close-up at 47°; soft rounded rendering.
CAMERA: Shots 1 and 3 static, lens at the height of the cat's shoulders; Shot 2 static, lens level with the lever and close enough that the lever fills the frame's height.
ACTION: SHOT 1 (0.0–4.0 s): the cat lands on the floorboards, shakes rain off in two shakes — droplets catch the window light — then looks up at the lamp. HARD CUT; the cat's pose at the end of Shot 1 exactly matches its start in Shot 2. SHOT 2 (4.0–7.0 s): the cat rears up and pushes the brass lever with both forepaws and its whole body weight; the lever tips up with one heavy clunk; only then a warm glow blooms from above. HARD CUT. SHOT 3 (7.0–10.0 s): the cat settles onto its haunches in the amber light, eyes widening, ears rising, and goes still.
LIGHTING: Shot 1 one cold key from the windows screen-right, 8500K, low exposure, the cat's far side in shadow; from the ignition in Shot 2 a warm 3200K top light, brighter than the window key, contact shadows under the cat.
AUDIO: <rain on glass, continuous> <two wet shakes> <one heavy metallic clunk at 6.0 s> <low warm hum from the lamp from 6.0 s> No music, no BGM — room tone and effects only.
ENDING STATE: cat seated on its haunches facing the lit lamp, lever up, room in warm amber, rain continuing on the glass.
STYLE: stylized 3D animated-feature look, matte rendered materials, soft global illumination; clean, grain-free image.
POSITIVE LOCKS: exactly one cat in every frame.
```
The attachment list lives in the slate's `Inputs` row, never inside the prompt (SKILL rule 11).

records.title: 3b. Sequence take S1 (shots 1A+1B) — technique A, Caption Spine — the technique this project chose (checklist steps 3–6; video-prompting ch. 12h; SKILL.md Economy and division of labour)
records.text:
```
Create a 10-second stylized 3D animated short inside the dark lamp room of a lighthouse on a rainy night.
STYLE: matte rendered materials, soft global illumination, cold window light, wet reflective floorboards, shallow depth of field, hushed mood, slow deliberate motion, room-tone sound.
@cat is a small grey tabby cat with wet clumped fur, a white chest patch, green eyes and a notch in its left ear. Keep the cat visually consistent throughout.
@anchor_1A is the exact background and the opening composition: the brass lever on the right wall, the half-open hatch on the left wall, rain-streaked windows and the unlit lamp above. @anchor_1B is the exact framing of the lever insert.
Camera: low, at the height of the cat's shoulders, looking across the floorboards toward the lever; the camera holds still.
0–4 s, medium-wide: the cat drops from the hatch onto the floorboards, shakes the rain off and looks up at the lamp; the lever stays down; rain drums on the glass.
4–7 s, close-up on the lever: the cat rears into frame and pushes the lever with its forepaws and its whole body until the lever tips up with a heavy clunk, and a warm glow blooms from above.
7–10 s, medium-wide: the cat settles onto its haunches and looks up at the lamp; its ears rise and it goes still; a low hum joins the rain.
End with the cat seated and still beneath the lamp, the room warm amber.
No dialogue, no subtitles, no text, no music. Maintain the same look throughout.
```
What is deliberately NOT in this prompt, and why: no OPTICS/FOV, no camera distance, no Kelvin, no PHYSICS block, no POSITIVE LOCKS — those axes are the model's (Division of labour); the lever's start state and the return to the medium-wide are each said once, inside the beat they belong to; the anchors carry the geography, so the beats never re-describe the room; the only negation is the closing sentence. If a run pushes with the head instead of the flank, the first repair step is still REMOVE (is anything on the push stated twice, or on an axis the model owns?), the second changes the half-sentence in beat two ("pushes the lever with its flank"), only the third adds one (SKILL rule 15).

records.title: 4. Sequence take S2 (shots 1C+1D) — extension round in the Caption Spine (video-prompting ch. 14b, 12h; mode routing first)
records.text:
```
Extend @Video 1 forward for 10 seconds, directly continued from its last frame: the seated cat beneath the lit lamp, the lever up, the room warm amber, rain on the glass.
STYLE: matte rendered materials, soft global illumination, warm lamp light, wet reflective floorboards, shallow depth of field, hushed mood, slow deliberate motion, room-tone sound.
@cat is the same small grey tabby cat with wet clumped fur, a white chest patch and green eyes. Keep the cat visually consistent throughout.
@loc_lamproom_rev is the exact background of the second shot, the room seen from the lamp side.
0–4 s, medium: the cat blinks slowly in the warm light and breathes out; its tail settles; the low hum and the rain continue.
4–10 s, wide from the lamp side, low: the beam begins a slow rotation overhead and its sweep passes across the cat's face; the cat's ears lift and it follows the beam with its eyes; a slow mechanical turning joins the hum.
End with the cat watching the turning beam and a slow fade to black.
No dialogue, no subtitles, no text, no music. Maintain the same look throughout.
```
The lever is fixed once, in the boundary sentence; `@prop_lever` is not attached because nothing about the lever changes in this round (12b tag rule: no tag for an object with no job). The counter-angle is carried by `@loc_lamproom_rev` and the shot-size words — no second camera line.
On a model without an extension mode (Seedance 2.0 and others): harvest S1's last clean frame as the literal start frame (the chain case, SKILL rule 1), keep Shot 1 on that angle, place the counter-angle as internal Shot 2 after the HARD CUT — in the project's technique, unchanged.

## 5. QA and log (production-pipeline ch. 10 · post-audio-legal ch. 17–19 · SKILL rules 13, 15)
Draft batch of 4 (`…__T2V__P01__TK01–TK04`, 720p), watched fully — by the director when the agent cannot view the result — in six passes (identity → continuity → timing → camera → audio → style/Verify line), verdict order post-audio-legal ch. 19 (hard rejects → rank by emotion → repair local faults). Failure example: TK02 renders the lever already up at 4.0 s → a hard continuity fault in a rejected take; TK02 is one bad roll of four (rule 15) — the prompt is not touched; only if three or four of the four rolls failed on the lever state would `…__T2V__P02` follow, in the rule-15 order — first REMOVE (is the lever stated twice, or anything written on an axis the model owns?), then CHANGE the half-sentence 'the lever stays down' inside beat one, add only third; the word count does not rise. TK03 approved at draft tier → the draft batch sits; the production take follows (§3c: same prompt, 1080p, TK05–TK08), TK07 approved → its Render ID with its Take ID becomes the shot board's `Approved-take Render ID` (`…__T2V__P01` (TK07)); from now on every local fault on TK07 is a `video_edit` (new Take ID), never a reroll. Grading, trim (±0.5 s, assembled cut only), score and loudness (−14 LUFS) in post.
