Build the reference POOL as a deliverable (ch. 14b) = the bible's asset registry (section B3): wardrobe details, prop stills, style stills, motion clips, voice/audio refs, clay blockouts — one reference for every element that must stay consistent anywhere, each row carrying its reference class (@Image / @Video / @Audio / @Clay Render).
5. Register everything as named elements with EXACT tag names (@hero, @loc_x, @anchor_1A); a name mismatch silently unbinds (production-pipeline ch. 5b; token form per surface: video-prompting ch. 12b) — and so does a missing one: the handle must stand as its literal `@token` in the prompt TEXT; an attached image referred to as "the reference image" does not bind, slot or no slot (style-control §7 Rule 0b).
6. Lock gate per LEAD asset (recurring characters, hero locations, hero props): ten-of-ten stress test (production-pipeline ch. 3 — ten generations with the sheet attached, varied pose and light, recognisable in ten of ten; run as image-model stills at draft tier — the cheap form — a fail means the description/sheet is wrong, not the model: fix and re-run). Only after it passes may the bible status move approved → locked (user approval still required, bible rule 3); cameos, extras and one-scene props stop at approved. The motion ladder is the STYLE/model gate and runs once per model in W7 step 4, not per asset.
Exit: every element the script needs exists as an approved, tagged reference; leads have passed the lock gate; bible asset registry updated.

records.title: W3 — Produce one shot (trigger: a numbered shot needs its first take)
records.text:
## W3 — Produce one shot (trigger: a numbered shot needs its first take)
1. CANON: read the beat in treatment/script/bible (rule 14: canon-bound vs craft-fillable content) — content before platform, same order as the per-prompt checklist.
2. ROUTE RECEIPT: mint or reuse the project KEY and write its RECEIPT line (SKILL.md Scope & version) in one of rule 17's two states — `live-checked <date>` when you or the user read the live form in THIS session, else `from reference <KEY>` with the stored key's own date. A from-reference receipt (rule 17) is enough to draft; live confirmation is the Generate-time gate, done by whoever has the form open. Do not choose controls until the receipt exists.
3. Lint the shot against `renderability.md` (red list §2, rescues §3) — rewrite or attach a rescue BEFORE spending a render.
4. Stills-first: generate the shot's still (per-prompt checklist; style mechanics per style-control §2–4 for the routed model) → user approves → register as `@anchor_<shot>`.
5. Draft batch — a BATCH OF 4 draft takes at draft resolution (480/720p, the take's planned length — 10 s by default; the motion test of production-pipeline ch. 1; ch. 10 batch protocol — watch all four fully: one odd take is a roll, four are the prompt) with the anchor attached as a tagged reference, take opening in motion (start-frame slot only for rule 1's two cases — say which path in the slate), the prompt in the project's technique (SKILL rule 4, from the bible frame) with its `Lint` row (video-prompting ch. 12h); judge with the project's Verify line (recipe's, or the default line from W1 step 5) + shot criteria (review loop, production-pipeline ch. 1; verdict order post-audio-legal ch. 19). When the agent cannot view the result, the director answers the six passes (SKILL checklist step 7). No bible (one-off prompt) → put the rule-4 menu to the director in one line, or ship `ASSUMED: technique = A` per the interaction contract and say so in the Intent row.
6. Production take only after the draft batch sits: target resolution, full duration — a new generation of the locked prompt (same Render ID, new settings row), not an extension of the draft take. The route decides what the target can be: over the Higgsfield API Seedance 2.5 renders 480p and 720p only (`HF-API@2026-09-18`) — a 1080p production take needs the web UI or an upscale (post-audio-legal ch. 17). **Exception to SKILL rule 13 (🟡 [PP]):** when the target-resolution generation loses scale or structure the draft had, route draft → scoped `video_edit` / upscale (W5, post-audio-legal ch. 17) instead of rerolling — a new Take ID (bible rule 3); offered, never forced, and draft pixels never go into the final. A defect accepted at the still stage propagates — surface that trade-off, the user decides.
Exit: approved take; anchor + statuses + render/take log rows in the bible.

records.title: W4 — Build a scene/sequence (trigger: several shots of one scene; anything longer than one take)
records.text:
## W4 — Build a scene/sequence (trigger: several shots of one scene; anything longer than one take)
1. Plan in shots (4–12 s), generate in takes: 1–3 internal shots per take (single shot for calm single-event beats, 2–3 only where a cut is needed for pace or coverage — production-pipeline ch. 2), every internal shot's anchor attached and time-scoped (production-pipeline ch. 1), explicit ENDING STATE, never a dramatic peak at a take's end (SKILL rule 2, ch. 14).
2. Chain takes with state chaining: each take's prompt begins from the previous ENDING STATE ("continue forward, do not replay"). Pick ONE join mechanism per model, never both for the same join: Seedance 2.5 → `video_extension` (30 s base + ONE extension round ≈60 s, boundary-frame contract each round from the last CLEAN frame of the raw export, then re-anchor a NEW generation from the original references — ch. 14b; no cold stitching, no harvested start frame; harvest the source's last frame only to WRITE the boundary state); models without a native extension mode (Seedance 2.0; check renderability §6 for others) → harvest the final frame as the next take's start frame — the chain case, rule 1's case (a) — case (b), the two-still interpolation, is the other; outside chained continuation the anchor is a reference, not a start frame (production-pipeline ch. 1).
3. Dialogue scenes: shot/reverse-shot with the multi-plate set + 180° lock (production-pipeline ch. 7; multi-plate set platforms-models ch. 13b); strongest lock = 3D blockout path (production-pipeline ch. 8). No recipe overrides the in-take axis lock (director-recipes header).
4. Assemble; the score is built in post — never in the video model (rule 10).
Exit: scene cut together from approved takes; continuity ledger (bible section B7) updated (ch. 19).

records.title: W5 — Repair a faulty take (trigger: a take that passed the hard rejects and won its batch by emotion — post-audio-legal ch. 19 verdict order — has a local fault)
records.text:
## W5 — Repair a faulty take (trigger: a take that passed the hard rejects and won its batch by emotion — post-audio-legal ch. 19 verdict order — has a local fault)
Seedance 2.5: never reroll an approved take for a local fault (rule 13) — route by the table. Other models: use the last three rows (Genjutsu on Higgsfield · no scoped edit route · global fault).
| Fault | Fix |
|---|---|
| Wrong object/face/detail in a region or time window | `video_edit`, region description + explicit time scope (ch. 14b/14) |
| Right performance, wrong camera | camera-perspective edit — segmented camera plan, everything else locked (ch. 14b); [PP]-unproven, one test, then rung 3 of W6 |
| Right performance, wrong environment | green-screen relocation via `omni_reference` (ch. 14b) |
| Wrong subject, right timeline | subject swap + Timeline Inheritance clause (ch. 14) |
| Audio only (music/voice/language/SFX) | audio-category edit — never touch pixels (ch. 14b) |
| Too short / scene continues | `video_extension` with boundary-frame contract (ch. 14b) |
| Wrong object, prop, wardrobe or location in an existing clip, any model's output, on Higgsfield | **Genjutsu — Object Swap** (Video → model selector → Genjutsu; one clip ≤30 s + up to 30 reference photos, output ≤1080p; `HF-WEB@2026-09-04`, changelog 2026-09-01) — untested here [🟡]; confirm the live form and treat the result as a new Take ID |
| Model/surface has no scoped edit route for this fault (Seedance 2.0, Kling, Veo, Grok; check the model's quick profile, renderability §6, and the surface in platform-ui-workflows — Runway = Aleph 2.0 Edit Studio, H3 = V2V edit) | harvest clean 2–4 s as coverage (production-pipeline ch. 10), fix the weakest instruction in the rule-15 order (remove → change → add), regenerate; `extend` only where the model offers it (Veo 3.1, Seedance) |
| Fault is global (style, light, physics everywhere) | back to the prompt in the rule-15 order — REMOVE first (every line on an axis the model owns and every second mention of a thing), CHANGE one line second, ADD only third; the word count never rises — then regenerate (production-pipeline ch. 1 review loop) |
Constraints (ch. 14b): source ≤20 s recommended, 1–5 refs; edits bill the source's full duration; ≤3 edit rounds per source, then branch from the best intermediate .mov export as the new @Video 1 (ch. 14b edit-round ceiling). Every edit result is a new Take ID (bible rule 3).
Exit: fixed take approved; its RECEIPT KEY and render/take log row noted in the bible.

records.title: W6 — Get a new angle / coverage (trigger: a reverse, insert, or B-camera view is needed on an EXISTING take, an approved still set or a filmed clip; planned reverse plates for dialogue/cross-room sets are pre-production → W2 step 3)
records.text:
## W6 — Get a new angle / coverage (trigger: a reverse, insert, or B-camera view is needed on an EXISTING take, an approved still set or a filmed clip; planned reverse plates for dialogue/cross-room sets are pre-production → W2 step 3)
Climb the ladder, exhaust each rung (ch. 16):
1. New angles as internal shots of the SAME take (cheapest, most reliable).
2. Harvest frames from an existing successful generation as references (last frame + "continue forward, do not replay"); or ONE camera-perspective edit on the approved take (B-camera pass — [PP]-unproven, budget one test only, bills the source's full duration; ch. 16 rung 2, ch. 14b). A filmed clip takes the same two routes — edit keeps its timing, reference re-creates the scene (ch. 16 rung 2). A failed single test → rung 3, not a second edit.
3. Still needed as a STILL: a purpose-built angle tool IF the live Higgsfield shell has one (production-pipeline ch. 16 tool section: undated, verify in the tool picker and mint a fresh receipt first) or GPT Image 2.5 WITH a layout map — never free-text "same scene from behind". Reverse test: anchors, openings, light side, palette against the master plate.
4. Nothing pins → geometry inputs: 3D blockout/clay render (production-pipeline ch. 8; video-prompting ch. 14b).
Exit: coverage that passes the reverse test.

records.title: W7 — Define & lock a style (trigger: user names a director/film/mood, or the look drifts)
records.text:
## W7 — Define & lock a style (trigger: user names a director/film/mood, or the look drifts)
1. User names a direction → `director-recipes.md` selection index; cap = ONE director recipe + at most ONE DoP signature (two packages, one dominant); two directors named → synthesis (selection index step 6), never two recipes side by side.
2. Build the project style anchor (the style-contract paragraph) from look-defining references via LLM reverse-engineering (style-control §7), or from the vocabulary packages (style-control §6) — plus its look tokens (8–10 for a Caption Spine, 4–8 for the block structure, none in technique C — SKILL.md Workflow step 4).
3. Stylized 3D: figure anchor or style-forcing blocks (SKILL rule 9; pixar-look §8/§9).
4. Validate on ONE still + one motion-ladder test per model before rolling out (style-control §5b); the recipe's Verify line becomes the standing reroll gate (replacing a DEFAULT line from W1 step 5).
5. Write the final style anchor + look tokens into the bible (section B2); from then on it is canon, distributed into every prompt per SKILL.md Workflow step 4.
Exit: style anchor + look tokens + Verify line in the bible + a passing verify still.

records.title: W8 — A generation keeps failing (trigger: one prompt has failed on the same axis on a full batch of 4, or two iterations in a row)
records.text:
## W8 — A generation keeps failing (trigger: one prompt has failed on the same axis on a full batch of 4, or two iterations in a row)
1. Suspect the PROMPT first (in first-party production sessions [PP, 🟡 heuristic, not a measured statistic] roughly 8 of 10 presumed model limits were prompt faults, SKILL rule 15): **for a STILL prompt count the words against the routed model+version's budget BEFORE reading the text** — past the budget, instructions that are present and correct are dropped silently, which is the single cheapest fault to miss (ch. 24b item 8; a video prompt has no house word ceiling) — then suspect OVER-instruction first (economy doctrine): read the seven `Lint` measures off the failed prompt and strip every sentence on an axis the model owns (SKILL.md Division of labour) and every second mention before anything else — then lint for internal contradictions, missing positive lock on the failing axis, stacked instructions on one axis, meta commentary (ch. 24b). Stills: run the eight-check lint (ch. 24i).
2. Count and repair per SKILL rule 15 (iteration = batch of 4 · remove → change → add · 3 failed iterations = short rewrite + channel change · 2 clean failures = model limit · 10–15 iterations = simplify the shot); routes: other model renderability §6, rescue §3, kept risk into the register (rule 11).
Exit: working result, or a documented model limit with a rescue.

records.title: W9 — Session open & close (trigger: every working session in an existing project)
records.text:
## W9 — Session open & close (trigger: every working session in an existing project)
Open: load the production bible FIRST (rule 12) — its frame decisions (model stack, look, prompting technique: rule 4) are the session's constants; read only the files the active runbook step names; revalidate the RECEIPT line (SKILL.md Scope & version; state per SKILL rule 17) for every active generation route before relying on a control.
Close: run the `[edit]`-tagged assembly checks of the project's Verify line on the assembled cut (director-recipes; they never gate a reroll); then update the bible LAST — add each actual generation/edit's KEY and render/take log row (section B4b) to the shot board and the delivery's Render Slates; statuses only on user approval, decisions as canon, open risks into the shot board's Risk → rescue cell (copied from the delivery risk registers); reviews the agent could not perform as `TKnn — review pending (director)` in Handoff; nothing outside the bible is canon. Offer ONCE per project (bible decision log: `feedback-to-skill offer: made / declined`) to feed genuinely new production findings back to the public skill (generalized, no project content — SKILL.md closing section).

records.title: W10 — Storyboard-first production model (trigger: a new project adopts the storyboard-first model; "how do we go about this"; any project with more than one camera axis per location, vertical geography, or a documented geography drift between takes)
records.text:
## W10 — Storyboard-first production model (trigger: a new project adopts the storyboard-first model; "how do we go about this"; any project with more than one camera axis per location, vertical geography, or a documented geography drift between takes)
Nine gated stages (stage 4, the animatic, is optional — the director may skip it on a short single-axis project; record the skip in the decision log). Each stage names its **Deliverable**, its **Gate** (what must exist before the next stage starts — a gate not passed means the next stage does not start) and its **Reads** (the only files opened in that stage). W10 adds no rules of its own: every rule it applies lives in the chapter it cites (production-pipeline ch. 1 build order, ch. 3 anchor standard, ch. 8 blockout trigger, ch. 9 storyboard roles, ch. 2 deliverable shape; production-take exception W3 step 6); W10 fixes the ORDER in which W1–W3 and W7 run and inserts the three planning artefacts (camera setup system, take/cut table, timed animatic) the later stages consume.

1. **Idea & brainstorming** — the director brings the idea; the agent moderates (story intake gate story-structures 23a, container offer 23f, causal change lint 23g). Reads: `genre-baselines.md` if a genre is named, `story-structures.md` 23a/23f/23g. Deliverable: logline + beat chain as a DRAFT proposal (SKILL rule 14), every beat written cause→effect (rule 16). Gate: the director confirms the logline AND the beat chain; an unconfirmed beat is not drawn in stage 3.
2. **Project briefing / bible** — create the bible (production-bible 22b) with story, look contract (W7 if a style is named), character/location/prop list (names + planned statuses), format, length, platform, model stack (W1 steps 3–5). Reads: `production-bible.md` 22a/22b, `renderability.md` §2–3, W1. Then the **renderability lint of the briefing**: classify EVERY beat against the renderability §2 rows — in particular "Physics as hero", "Tiny hero object", "Dark, figure-less macro", "Continuous approach over distance", "Cut back onto the same emissive object", "Long continuous camera moves", "Wide shots". Every red beat receives an ellipsis or still rescue (renderability §3) or is cut — BEFORE the storyboard. Why: these beat classes are the documented time-eaters; a storyboard that draws them plans shots that never come out. Deliverable: bible B1–B3 filled, beat-level risk register (SKILL rule 11 shape; the director's decision is written into `Why kept`). Gate: bible exists; no beat is red without a decided rescue.
3. **Storyboard = shot planning** — deliver the STORYBOARD of production-pipeline ch. 2, all four parts: (1) camera setup system per location, (2) look-free panels with setup tags and a/b pairs, (3) take/cut table with the state ladder, (4) layout map — and the ranking stated there (setup system + table + ladder + anchors bind; panels are the director's checking view). Reads: `production-pipeline.md` ch. 2 (shape, rules, export schema), ch. 4 (the setup system IS the reverse decision), ch. 8 (layout map), ch. 9 (storyboard roles; grey sketch template); `film-craft.md` for coverage grammar. Tool: **FilmFlow Pro** (`FILMFLOW-WEB@2026-09-07`, platform-ui-workflows ledger) is the recommended environment for stages 2–3 IF (a) its frames stay look-free (sketch/clay, no rendered look) and (b) it yields an agent-readable export in the production-pipeline ch. 2 schema; otherwise a Markdown shot board + grey image-model sketches. Gate: director sign-off on all four parts; the storyboard is linked in bible section B3b with version and sign-off date. From here every prompt is written from panel + setup line + take row — never from prose.
4. **Animatic — timing & montage simulation (OPTIONAL, before the sheets)** — play the storyboard as a TIMED reel to test montage, order, rhythm, causality and per-shot duration BEFORE any consistency asset is built. Each panel (or a/b pair) is held for its take-table `Len`; scratch audio (VO + temp music + timing markers) sets the true minimum durations — dialogue length is only real once spoken (SKILL rule 2: the take's `Len` is where this locks). Why HERE, before the sheets: the animatic needs NO final designs — only the load-bearing aspects of figures and locations sketched, i.e. the look-free panels stage 3 already produced (production-pipeline ch. 9 storyboard roles). Running it first is a GATE that kills, merges, reorders or shortens shots before sheet and render budget is spent on them — and the R3 rung below doubles as the earliest warning system for exactly the red-list beats (fast motion, hero physics, `Physics as hero`) flagged in stage 2, the beats most expensive to fix late. **Fidelity ladder — chosen PER BEAT (not per project); escalate only as far as the beat's open question demands:**
   - **R1 — held still + scratch audio:** order, duration, dialogue timing. Zero cost, the default rung.
   - **R2 — deterministic camera on the still** (Ken Burns push/pan/zoom, dissolves; or a first→last-frame interpolation between two panels of THIS shot — the SKILL rule 1 controlled move, not a performance): tests camera timing, reveals, cut rhythm. Deterministic, no drift, no model cost, re-editable (NLE / ffmpeg `zoompan`).
   - **R3 — sub-shot panels** (higher temporal resolution of one shot: several drawings per shot, played flip-book): tests action/motion timing for fast or complex beats — does the beat fit its seconds, or must it be split/elided (renderability §3). Three interchangeable ways to produce the in-betweens, all feeding the same reel: hand- or AI-drawn intermediate panels (deterministic, no model); cheap image-gen in the same rough sketch style; or a cheap low-res tween (480p, an old video model) / interpolation between two panels.
     - **R3 discipline (binding):** the in-betweens illustrate the ACTION PROGRESSION and TIMING only — never the performance, the optics, or the identity. Read duration and beat-fit; discard the model's specific motion. Letting a cheap tween's motion become canon plans the shot against motion the production model will not reproduce (a timing test laundered into false canon).

   Reads: `production-pipeline.md` ch. 2 (take/cut table + state ladder — the animatic PLAYS this), ch. 9 (storyboard roles; panels stay look-free); `film-craft.md` (editing, rhythm, coverage grammar); `renderability.md` §2–3 (the red beats the R3 rung stress-tests). Tool: FilmFlow Pro (`FILMFLOW-WEB@2026-09-07`, platform-ui-workflows ledger) already binds panels to shots with animatic playback and per-shot timing and fits R1/R2 directly (the same surface used for stages 2–3); otherwise an NLE or ffmpeg `zoompan`. For an R3 tween a cheap video route at 480p — mint a receipt first (SKILL rule 17). Deliverable: a timed animatic reel + a **revised take/cut table** — `Len` values locked or corrected, internal-shot counts decided (SKILL rule 2: calm beat = 1 shot; dynamic/dialogue = 2–3 cuts), continuity/causality flags raised (rule 16). Gate: director sign-off on the reel; the corrected `Len` and cut points are written back into the storyboard (B3b) and the take/cut table (B4) BEFORE the sheets start. The animatic never becomes a look reference and its R3 motion is never canon — it corrects timing and cut points, nothing else.
5. **Character & prop sheets (Elements)** — BEFORE the blockout: build-order case (c) of production-pipeline ch. 1 (the blockout needs the proportions; body length is the scale unit of the layout map — a numeric channel (SKILL rule 7); in prose scale stays a relation). W2 steps 2, 5 and 6 per character; prop sheets and state pairs per the state ladder (production-pipeline ch. 4). Iterate every sheet to the **anchor standard** (production-pipeline ch. 3: exact, never "good enough"). Reads: `production-pipeline.md` ch. 1 (order), ch. 3–4, `style-control.md` for the routed still model, W2. Gate: sheets approved (leads through the W2 step-6 lock gate), scale written as object relations in B3 (production-pipeline ch. 4).
6. **3D blocking / blockout** — the production-pipeline ch. 8 blockout, run as a stage under the **blockout trigger rule** (production-pipeline ch. 8: optional for one axis + flat geography, mandatory for vertical geography, several axes, or documented drift): one scene per location, every panel placed as a camera on it; viewport render per the production-pipeline ch. 8 blockout-video requirements (24 fps, overlays off, 3–5 s per move, ≈30 s reference budget) as the `@Clay Render` staging reference — role split blockout = camera/blocking/timing, images = look (production-pipeline ch. 8 mandatory companions). Tool-neutral (production-pipeline ch. 8 evidence tiers; Blender + Bridge MCP `HF-BRIDGE-MCP@2026-09-04` is the documented baseline). Reads: `production-pipeline.md` ch. 8, `video-prompting.md` ch. 14b (reference budgets, @Clay Render role line). Gate: blockout frames match the panels (framing, position, gaze direction); a mismatch is fixed in the blockout or marked on the panel — the panel is never redrawn to match the blockout.
7. **Location anchors** — plates AFTER the blockout (production-pipeline ch. 1 case (c)): the blockout frame or the layout schematic is the geography reference of the plate prompt, the look comes from the style contract (B2); light openings described as geometry per production-pipeline ch. 4. W2 step 3 and production-pipeline ch. 4 per location, one plate per setup that needs its own view. Storyboard panels never enter a generation (production-pipeline ch. 9 storyboard roles). Reads: `production-pipeline.md` ch. 4, `style-control.md`, W2 step 3. Gate: anchors exact (anchor standard, production-pipeline ch. 3) — light direction, scale, geography match the layout map.
8. **Draft takes at draft tier (720p)** — per take W3 steps 1–5: canon from panel + take row, receipt, lint, still anchor, batch of 4 at 720p; rule-15 iteration count. Reads: W3, W4 (chaining), W8 (failing), `video-prompting.md` ch. 12h / ch. 12 / style-control §6c per the project's technique (bible B1), ch. 14. Gate: the STRUCTURE of the take holds — cuts land on the take-table timecodes, continuity states in and out match, identities hold. Polish is not judged here.
9. **Production takes (1080p / 4K)** — W3 step 6: a new generation of the locked prompt at target resolution by default; its documented exception (draft → `video_edit` / upscale when the reroll loses scale or structure) applies as written there. Never cut draft pixels into the final: the draft cut fixes structure, not pixels. Then picture lock → audio → grade as dated stages (post-audio-legal ch. 17/18; dates in B6, state in B8). Reads: W3 step 6, W5, `post-audio-legal.md` ch. 17–19.
Exit: storyboard, setup system and take/cut table in the bible as canon (B3b, B4 columns filled); every shot at status ≥ take; picture lock dated.

**W10 house rules** (each lives in the chapter named; listed here so a session sees them together):
- Anchor standard — iterate until exact, deadline pressure does not lower it (production-pipeline ch. 3).
- A post-state needs a visible cause in frame — break point, debris, crack — or it reads as placed (state ladder, production-pipeline ch. 2; state pairs, production-pipeline ch. 4).
- Continuity between takes = the join mechanism of W4 step 2 (keeper's end frame per rule 1) + a position lock over all internal shots + one axis (production-pipeline ch. 6 position lock).
- Scale only as object relations, never adjectives (production-pipeline ch. 4; image-model-logic 24b).
- Light openings as geometry; light-geometry words generate rays (production-pipeline ch. 4).
- Actions as two states; an uninvolved object or a gaze direction is written only when the canon demands it or a run of this take has shown it drifting (production-pipeline ch. 6 position lock).
- Panels from an image model are independent inventions — consistency comes from the setup system on paper and the blockout in geometry; the storyboard says WHAT must stay the same, the blockout says HOW (production-pipeline ch. 9 storyboard roles).
- A storyboard without a camera setup system is unusable — free camera positions per panel produce the perspective inconsistency that later shows up in the takes (production-pipeline ch. 2).
- A storyboard is canon only when linked in the bible (section B3b); a document beside the bible is ignored by the next session.

records.title: AI Film Production
records.text:
| The model owns by default — nothing is written here unless deliberately steered | The agent always owns — exactly this is written |
|---|---|
| camera composition inside a named shot size · in-take cutting and cut timing · character motion and body mechanics · material rendering · light behaviour and falloff · transitions · the physics of simple contact actions | what is in the scene · what happens in which order, and the state each beat ends in · which reference carries which single job · canon fidelity (the written beat) · one camera line where continuity across internal cuts requires it |

records.title: Task routing — which file is the spine for which task
records.text:
| Task at hand | Spine — read the named part, not the whole file |
|---|---|
| Resume a running project; "where were we"; project state, asset registry, shot status | `references/production-bible.md` — the project's bible, then only what the active runbook step names |
| New project with a genre named or evident ("action film", "horror short", "doc-style" …) | `references/genre-baselines.md` — craft defaults, recipe shortlist, per-genre file filters |
| A story or idea needs its dramaturgical shape; story completeness check | `references/story-structures.md` — intake gate 23a, container library, causal change lint 23g |
| Write, fix or review ANY video prompt | `references/workflows.md` W3 (W4 scene, W5 repair) → the project's technique chapter (rule 4; filled examples worked-example.md §3b for A, §3 for B) → ch. 14–14b; the checklist then pulls the platform receipt and `renderability.md` §2–3. A fix/review returns: verdict line → numbered findings (quoted line → problem → change) → the rewritten prompt as a Render Slate — never a silent rewrite; the first finding looked for is over-instruction (rule 15) |
| Prompt syntax for H3 / Kling / Veo / Grok (not live UI controls) | `references/platforms-models.md` ch. 21 (copy-ready instance per model) + `references/video-prompting.md` 12g — verify the live syntax before a paid run |
| A live UI/MCP/API surface, setting, mode, limit, receipt or learning link for Higgsfield / fal.ai / Runway / OpenArt / Arcads / ChatGPT | `references/platform-ui-workflows.md` — §0, then the platform's § (§6 when choosing between platforms); the archived Cinema 3.5 table (platforms-models ch. 13) is never a current selector list |
| Treatment, script, shot list; asset orders (sheets, plates, props); still-model choice; QA batches; reverse angles and coverage; a new camera angle on an existing clip, generated or filmed | `references/production-pipeline.md` — deliverable shapes ch. 2, asset order ch. 3, model matrix ch. 5, QA ch. 10, coverage ladder ch. 16 |
| Any stylized look; any prompt that uses reference images; image-model mechanics | `references/style-control.md` — §2 GPT Image 2.5 · §3 Nano Banana Pro · §4 Soul Cinema/Seedream · §5b medium motion grammar · §6c medium-emulation packages and the Master Style Block (technique C) · §7 reference integration |
| Position, size, count or exclusion problems in image prompts; a model "ignoring" an instruction | `references/image-model-logic.md` ch. 24 — writing contract 24b, control ladders 24c–e, negation channels 24f, edits 24g, still-prompt lint 24i |
| Feasibility lint of a script or shot; assign models; rescue risky action; lighting consistency | `references/renderability.md` — answer shape under §2, rescues §3, lighting §5b, model profiles §6 |
| Cinematography, editing, light, colour or dramaturgy advice; "how should this scene feel" | `references/film-craft.md` |
| A style starting point; a director or DoP is named | `references/director-recipes.md` — selection index, then the named recipe; each closes on a Verify line |
| Pixar / stylized-3D projects | `references/pixar-look.md` — figure-anchor rule §8, figure-less method §9, previs-to-AI case study §10 |
| Post, upscaling, music and voices, continuity ledger, legal and AI disclosure, real-face moderation, take verdict order | `references/post-audio-legal.md` — ch. 19 holds the binding verdict order and the six review passes |
| The storyboard-first production model; "how do we go about this"; storyboard, camera setup system, take/cut table, animatic or blockout stage | `references/workflows.md` W10 — nine gated stages from idea to production takes |
| Which model to run a session, a subagent or a batch on; handing skill work to another agent | `references/agent-models.md` — measured cold-test results per model, what to delegate and what never, the cold-test protocol |
| First production task ever; a term is ambiguous | `references/worked-example.md` (one complete delivery in both techniques) · `references/glossary.md` (one meaning per term) |

records.title: The Render Slate — delivery wrapper for every executable prompt
records.text:
| Row | Content |
|---|---|
| `Render ID` | `<PROJECT>_<Shot ID>__<platform-model>__<operation>__P<nn>` (ID discipline below) |
| `Intent` | One director-readable line: shot, action, decisive creative constraint; opens with `Canon: DRAFT — approve the treatment before running` when the treatment is not yet approved (rule 14) |
| `Crew choices` | Two halves. *Left to the model:* the axes this prompt deliberately does not instruct. *Decided by the crew:* the craft-fillable decisions the canon did not fix, every look control included — the director's veto list (rule 14). Example: `Left to the model: composition inside the shot sizes, cut timing, body mechanics, wet fur and brass, the light bloom. Decided by the crew: medium-wide → close-up → medium-wide; one camera line, low at the cat's shoulder height, looking toward the lever; the rain shake as the reaction cue.` |
| `Run in` | The RECEIPT chain platform → access route → project/workspace → surface/tool → model → mode as `id ("UI label")`, then the KEY and its receipt state (rule 17). Example: `Higgsfield → web UI → project LIGHTCAT → Video → Seedance 2.5 → t2v (UI label unverified — read the live task dropdown) — from reference HF-WEB@2026-09-04, not live-checked this session; confirm model, mode and workspace on the live form before Generate` |
| `Settings` | Executable UI values: ratio, resolution, duration, audio, any non-default control. Never repeat a UI setting inside a video prompt — no double control (exceptions: the take's duration where the technique's form carries it; a control the project's A/B proved inert, platform-ui-workflows §1; the Higgsfield DoP tool, production-pipeline ch. 16). Still prompts keep the canvas/aspect/grid line in the prompt, first, AND set it in the UI (style-control §2) |
| `Lint` | Every video prompt, in any technique: `words n · negations n/1 · numerals outside TC n/0 · absolute measures n/0 · double mentions none · contradictions none · beats complete` (definitions and counting rules: ch. 12h; `words` is a count for the rule-15 ratchet, never a ceiling; each numeral exception is a look control named in Crew choices) |
| `Inputs` | One line per reference, numbered in slot/upload order: `n. @tag = what it is — its one job`; say whether the anchor is a reference or a literal start/end frame (rule 1); on a platform with a persistent library say "Elements, no upload"; add `🟡 token form unverified — match the upload label before running` when the surface could not be seen (ch. 12b) |
| `Store in` | Known platform project/folder or local destination — omit rather than invent |
| `Handoff` | Linked work only: an extension boundary state, an edit source + scope (`edit source …__T2V__P01__TK03`), a continuity boundary |

| romantic, longing, memory of love | Wong Kar-wai (+ Doyle) · Malick (+ Lubezki) |

records.title: Selection index: brief → recipe
records.text:
| Project constraint | Favors | Penalizes |
|---|---|---|
| Low reroll budget / tight deadline | Malick (mosaic of short moments), Boyle (montage), Ozu (locked frontal statics), Gilligan (wordless process montage) | Tarkovsky, Lubezki-style oners — long coherent takes mean extension chains + high reroll cost |
| Complex action, crowds, physics risk | Greengrass, UGC, Lynch — absorb or legitimize artifacts; Kurosawa — telephoto crowd planes + weather cover | Fincher, Kubrick — surgical frames expose every flaw |
| Dialogue-heavy | Ozu (frontal singles sidestep reverse-angle continuity), Tarantino, Bergman | Greengrass — verité dialogue coverage burns takes |
| Film lives on face performance | Bergman + Nykvist — spend the reroll budget here | Willis (buried eyes), heavy-silhouette styles |
| High continuity risk (many locations/outfits/characters) | Malick, Lynch — elliptical/dream logic tolerates jumps | Nolan cross-cutting — parallel lines punish continuity errors |
| Stylized/animated format | Miyazaki, Anderson, Pixar → pixar-look.md | Fraser/Willis deep underexposure — clashes with readable-face warmth |

records.title: Selection index: brief → recipe
records.text:
| Named | Compile as | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Coppola (Godfather register) | Willis signature + Leone opera timing | Power geometry static and frontal; ritual cross-cut against violence (the baptism logic — Hitchcock's cross-cutting grammar) |
| Coppola (Apocalypse Now register) | Storaro signature + Malick's elliptical VO-journey structure | Color as ideology over a sensory drift downriver; war as hallucination |
| Cameron | Spielberg structure + Hoytema signature | Action geography even stricter than Spielberg — every cut preserves the map; steel-blue tech sublime; escalation engineered act by act |
| Jarmusch | Wenders structure + Müller signature + Ozu statics | Drier deadpan, longer holds; hangout, not journey |

records.title: Harmony map: which packages combine
records.text:
| Director recipe | DoP signature | Why it harmonizes |
|---|---|---|
| Spielberg | Kamiński | Blown godlight + smoke gives the wonder-and-threat grammar its sentiment and its war-memory grit — both extremes in one toolkit |
| Nolan | Hoytema | Monumental sober naturalism scales to IMAX mechanisms without gloss; cool restraint matches engineered structure |
| Villeneuve | Deakins → Fraser | Deakins built the monumental-clarity phase; Fraser's texture-first underexposure carries the later dust-and-dread scale — both serve duration-dread |
| Wong Kar-wai | Doyle | Step-printed neon smear IS the longing; structure and image are inseparable here — adopt them together or not at all |
| Bergman | Nykvist | The face-as-landscape structure needs the face-light standard; nothing decorative survives the chamber |
| Allen lineage | Willis | The amber NY period — master-shot talk in underexposed warm rooms; comedy that trusts darkness |
| Sciamma | Mathon | The gaze structure needs flame-and-dusk honesty; portrait stillness is shared doctrine |
| Malick | Lubezki | Wandering whisper-montage requires a camera that lives in natural light and moves like breath |
| Wenders | Müller | Available-light Americana trust — the seeing-road structure needs a camera that treats neon and dusk as sufficient |
| Gilligan | (Michael Slovis / BCS lineage) | Hard-sun neo-western wides, object-POV wit, and time-lapse punctuation were built WITH the house camera department — the image grammar is part of the recipe; no full second package |
| Kubrick / Tarantino / Fincher / Scorsese / Ridley Scott / Wright / Wachowskis | (house signatures) | Their image grammar is baked into the director recipe itself — no external DoP package needed; adding one dilutes |

records.title: 2. Composition
records.text:
| Tool | Effect | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| Rule of thirds | Natural, balanced | Default; subject on a power point, gaze into open space |
| Central/symmetric | Formal, controlled, confrontational or comic | Authority, ritual, deadpan; breaks feel deliberate |
| Leading lines | Steers the eye | Reveals, depth, connecting subject↔goal |
| Frame-in-frame | Isolation, voyeurism, entrapment | Doorways, windows, mirrors-as-shape (not reflections) |
| Negative space | Loneliness, insignificance, dread | Small subject vs. big empty area; horror off-screen space |
| Headroom/lead room | Comfort norms | Break them (crowded headroom, no lead room) for unease |
| Depth layering | Immersion, scale | Always name FG/MG/BG (ties into location plates) |
| High vs. low horizon | Sky = fate/freedom; ground = weight/burden | Establishings, emotional wides |
| Balance/imbalance | Stability vs. tension | Tilt/dutch and asymmetry signal "something is wrong" |

records.title: 3. Camera: position, angle, movement, lens
records.text:
| Move | Reads as | Motivated by |
|---|---|---|
| Static/locked | Observation, tension, dignity | Letting performance play; dread (what moves inside the frame?) |
| Pan/tilt | Attention shift | Following gaze or subject |
| Dolly in | Rising importance, realization | Emotional intensification (slow) or threat (fast) |
| Dolly out | Abandonment, context reveal, ending | Loss, punchline reveals, closing shots |
| Tracking/lateral | Accompaniment, parallel life | Walk-and-talks, journeys |
| Crane/rise | Overview, transcendence, epilogue | Openings/closings, scale reveals |
| Handheld | Presence, nervousness, documentary truth | Subjectivity, chaos — dose it, don't default |
| Orbit | Inspection, disorientation, iconization | Hero moments, revelations; expensive — earn it |
| Zoom (vs dolly) | Artificial attention, period flavor | 70s look, crash-zoom comedy/doc |
| Crash zoom in / out | Shock, sudden realisation, comic emphasis (in); absurd context reveal, punchline (out) | A discovery or a gag beat — the 70s / Kill Bill register [P59] |
| Snorricam / body mount | Panic, intoxication, dissociation — the head locked, the world lurching | Subjective crisis; the worn-product shot (video-prompting 12e) [P59] |
| Earth zoom-out · infinite zoom · tilt-shift | From one human moment to the whole world · surreal reveal · model-world detachment | Openings, closings, dream and scale devices — cheap in AI, dose them [P59] |

records.title: 4. Editing
records.text:
| Cut | Function |
|---|---|
| Hard cut on action | Invisible continuity — cut mid-movement, the motion hides the seam |
| Match cut (graphic/motion) | Poetic linkage across space/time; scene transitions |
| Cut on look (eyeline) | Question → answer: face looks, next shot shows what they see (Kuleshov: the pairing CREATES the emotion) |
| J-cut (audio leads) | Pulls forward, smooth scene entry — sound of the next scene starts under the current one |
| L-cut (audio trails) | Reaction room — we watch listeners while the speaker continues |
| Jump cut | Time compression, nervous energy, comedy of repetition |
| Smash cut | Violent contrast (loud→silent, calm→chaos); comedy and shock |
| Cutaway/insert | Detail emphasis, tension objects, hiding continuity errors |
| Cross-cutting | Parallel action = suspense engine; alternate locations, tighten intervals toward collision |
| Ellipsis | Skip the unfilmable/boring; the audience's mind bridges (also the AI rescue tool, renderability) |
| Scene transitions | Sound bridge (audio crosses the cut — the workhorse) · match dissolve (time passing, memory) · hard black (chapter weight) · whip/wipe (playful momentum, period flavor) — pick ONE transition language per film |

records.title: 24f. Negation & exclusion — a channel decision, not a wording choice
records.text:
| Model class | Exclusion channel that works |
|---|---|
| Diffusion stills (FLUX, SD3.5, Midjourney, Imagen) | Dedicated negative field / `--no` only — bare atomic nouns ("people", "wall"), one concept per entry (compounds get split and over-exclude), NEVER "don't/no X" in the prompt body |
| AR/reasoning stills (GPT Image, Nano Banana) | Short in-prompt exclusions are vendor-endorsed ("no watermark, no extra text") and legitimate — but the positive description still carries the composition; Google's own rule: positive framing first ("empty street", not "no cars") |
| Video models | Ch. 14 negative rule governs (it's consistent with this research): Seedance takes in-prompt negations for subtitles, on-screen text and audio (official: "Use positive descriptions whenever possible. Negative constraints are supported for subtitles and audio control" [BD-off]), every other exclusion positive first; Veo/Kling use their negative fields with bare keywords, most critical first; models without a dedicated negative field → rewrite prohibitions as the desired state ("the boy waves his hands", not "can't stay still") |

records.title: 24g. Edits & locality
records.text:
| Mask type | Platforms | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Hard** (algorithmic clamp: outside-mask content mathematically preserved) | FLUX Fill (binary b/w mask), Imagen/Vertex inpaint (`maskDilation` ~0.01) | Content cannot escape; the mask truly defines region AND size |
| **Soft** (guidance only) | GPT Image `mask` param — official: "entirely prompt-based… may not follow its exact shape"; may repaint globally (documented on the `gpt-image-2` generation; re-verify on `gpt-image-2.5` — the 2.5 edit-precision claim above may change this) | Always pair with the full prompt-level preserve list; expect overflow |
| **No pixel mask** | Nano Banana API (semantic masking by prompt only); Seedream (annotation channel: boxes/arrows/coordinates/sketch instead); Higgsfield mask-brush UI over NB Pro (rough mask OK — expand slightly when replacing, widen + regenerate when an edit misses) | Use the platform's native channel; don't assume mask semantics that aren't there |

records.title: 24h. Quick reference — problem → first move → hard fix
records.text:
| Problem | First move (prompt-level) | Hard fix (channel change) |
|---|---|---|
| Place an element | Zone language early + named scene geometry | Layout sketch → structure map/annotation → composite layers |
| Set an element's size | Object-class word + shot type/lens + ONE relational anchor | Mask drawn at size (hard-mask platform) / sketch-at-size / composite |
| Small object with detail | Detail described at target scale | Crop-zoom-inpaint-paste-back |
| Exact count | One plain number ≤4, simple background | Multi-panel / scaffolded adds / crowd sheet |
| Exclude something | Positive replacement in the same slot | Negative field (diffusion) / short exclusion (AR) / accept-and-post fallback |
| Local edit, keep the rest | "Change only X" + repeated preserve list, ≤3 iterations | Hard mask (FLUX Fill/Imagen) or restart from original with combined instruction |
| Keep composition, change content | Reference + role line ("layout and light only") | FLUX Depth/Canny structure lock |
| Layout fights you twice | Reroll seed (diffusion) or switch to AR-class model | Any of the above — but change CHANNEL, not vocabulary (24b item 7) |
| Prompt grew across runs; correct instructions stop landing | Cut back inside the model+version word budget; replace, never append (24b item 8) | Rewrite short from scratch (SKILL rule 15), then change channel |
| Only the exceptions of an object class render | Name the class's default state positively, and first (counterweight sentence, 24a) | Scaffold: generate the ordinary field, add the exceptions as an edit |
| A banned element returns right after you shortened the Avoid list | Restore it from the protected world-rule subset; cut only volatile entries (24f) | Positive replacement in the same slot instead of the ban |
| An object renders at the wrong size or distance despite a stated measure | Replace the measure with ONE relation to a named in-frame object (24d rung 3, SKILL rule 7) | Mask / box / sketch at size — numeric channel, never prose |

records.title: Operating contract for an agent
records.text:
| Platform | What the user is actually using | Best interpretation for an agent |
|---|---|---|
| **Higgsfield** | A film-production workspace plus separate image/video/edit tools. Cinema Studio 4.0 exposes a cinematic control surface around selectable models. | Route a scene/project to Cinema Studio; put film grammar into its selectors and the story/action into the prompt. |
| **fal.ai** | A model/API marketplace. Its browser UI is a test bench whose form is generated from each endpoint’s schema. | Route to a named model endpoint and inspect its exact schema. Do **not** describe fal as a film editor or assume a common set of controls. |
| **Runway** | A creative suite with free-form Tool Mode, task-specific Apps, a conversational Agent, a node editor (Workflows), and a lightweight timeline. | Choose the surface first: single asset, a named task, conversational production, or reusable automation. |
| **OpenArt** | An aggregated creative suite: single-shot image/video tools, saved Characters/Worlds/Brand Kit, structured tools, and the chat-based Director. | Choose between a shot-level tool and Director; retain recurring assets in the platform library rather than re-describing them every time. |
| **Arcads** | A performance-marketing/UGC production platform: product assets, image/video models, AI Actors, scripts/voices, localization, an ad agent, and reusable node workflows. | Choose the ad-production surface first: hands-on Studio, a Talking/Animated Actor, B-roll, Translate, Mark Agent, or a Workflow. It is not a general cinematic-film studio. |
| **ChatGPT** | A conversational image-generation surface running **ChatGPT Images 2.5** (`gpt-image-2.5` family — model choice: 'ChatGPT native image generation'), plus an optional host for connected third-party MCP apps. | Use it for conversational still creation/editing and reference-guided iteration. ChatGPT-native image generation is not a video generator and does not inherit an MCP provider’s web UI. |

| **Higgsfield → Audio / Lipsync Studio / Relight / Colour Palette / Layers** | Separate specialist forms for voice, lip sync, video light/grade, and image decomposition/editing. | An Audio/Lipsync, Relight, grade, or Layer setting is not a generation-model field. Route the user to the specialist tool instead of stuffing the request into a T2V prompt. | `HF-WEB@2026-09-04 / named specialist tool` |
| **fal.ai → exact endpoint → Playground/Sandbox** | Only fields rendered from that endpoint’s current schema. An endpoint may offer a prompt, enum, seed, upload, mask, audio, or visual camera widget—or none of these. | No global fal “video settings,” Cinema-like studio controls, or endpoint parity. A field from `provider/model-A` cannot be proposed for `provider/model-B` without its schema. | `FAL-WEB@2026-09-04 / endpoint_id / schema retrieval date` |
| **Runway → Tool Mode / named App / Agent / Workflow node** | The selected surface owns the form: e.g. Gen-4 Image, Gen-4.5 video, Act-Two, Aleph Edit Studio, an App task form, or node ports. | An App capability is not automatically a Gen-4.5 option; Agent preference is not a reusable Tool Mode parameter; Gen-4 Image reference controls are not Gen-4.5 editing controls. | `RW-WEB@2026-09-04 / named surface / named model + mode` |
| **OpenArt → named tool → selected model → mode** | The Video/Image/Smart Shot/Edit/Director form selected by the user, plus saved assets. Its model picker can change the visible inputs. | A Start/End Frame, Smart Shot, Director, or Edit Video setting is not a universal “OpenArt Seedance” field, even when the same provider model name is displayed. | `OA-WEB@2026-09-04 / URL / selected model + mode` |
| **Arcads → Studio / AI Actor mode / B-roll / Translate / Mark / Workflow** | A product-ad control plane. Each route owns separate fields: image model/prompt, actor/voice/script/emotion, movement, B-roll model, locale/accent, conversational campaign brief, or nodes. | An Arcads actor, script emotion, subtitle, translation, or Workflow-node option is not a Seedance/FLUX/Cinema parameter—and an underlying video-model choice does not make all Arcads ad tools available in that model form. | `AR-WEB@2026-08-31 / named Arcads surface / active model or node` |
| **ChatGPT → ordinary chat → built-in image generation** | Natural-language prompt; attached reference image(s); conversational, targeted follow-up edits. The built-in route runs **ChatGPT Images 2.5** (`gpt-image-2.5` family). | It has no native video-generation route in this reference. Do not call a connector automatically and do not represent another provider’s model/mode/asset controls as native ChatGPT controls. | `CGPT-IMG@gpt-image-2.5@2026-09-09 / native chat` |

records.title: How an agent converts an artistic instruction into an actionable one
records.text:
| User intent | Correct action | Unsafe shortcut |
|---|---|---|
| “Make it a 1980s noir shot with a slow pan.” | In **Cinema Studio 4.0**, choose Era, Genre, and the visible movement preset; use the prompt for the event and concrete period props. | Claim that Seedance/FLUX/fal has those three selector values. |
| “Use this product image and preserve its label.” | Open the selected model/mode’s reference or image-input control and inspect its current limits; use a dedicated edit/region tool if the task is local replacement. | Assume every image/video model accepts references, masks, region edits, or text fidelity. |
| “Make the actor more fearful.” | In Cinema, use the Emotion Wheel with the actual `@Element`/character reference. Else write the performance intent in the prompt and say that it is not an equivalent control. | Offer the Cinema Emotion Wheel in a standalone Seedance, FLUX, fal, Runway, or OpenArt form. |
| “Change the grade/light after we like the take.” | Use Higgsfield Relight/Colour Palette or the selected platform’s dedicated video-edit tool. | Regenerate through a video model and promise a targeted non-destructive adjustment. |

records.title: Cinema Studio 4.0: what a user sets before generation
records.text:
| Panel / control | Verified current choices | What the agent should put there |
|---|---|---|
| **Genre** | General, Action, Epic, Drama, Comedy, Horror, Noir | Overall film logic/pacing. General leaves visual logic primarily to the prompt; do not also give contradictory genre directions in prose. |
| **Era** | Auto plus decade looks documented for 1960s, 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, 2020s; the product describes direct decade selection | Temporal capture/grade character, not plot period details that must appear as props/costume. |
| **Tempo / Montage Pacing** | Auto, Chaotic, Dynamic, Calm, Single Shot | Cut rhythm. Use **Single Shot** for one continuous take; do not promise an editable NLE timeline merely because the setting can generate cuts. |
| **Emotion Wheel** | Hope, Anger, Joy, Trust, Fear, Surprise, Sadness, Disgust; used with an `@character_name` tag | Performance for a named character, e.g. `@mara Fear`. It is not a general “make the whole film sad” knob. |
| **Colour Palette** | 50+ named templates; examples include Film Colors, Black Gloss, Candy Pink, Lime Jam, Nostalgic Blue | Colour/tonal direction. Use one deliberate choice and avoid countermanding it with a long incompatible colour recipe. |
| **Lighting** | Auto; Silhouette, Practicals, Window, Overhead Fall, Contre-jour, Soft Cross; manual colour, brightness, diffusion, angle | Source/direction of light. `Practicals` means visible in-frame sources; use it where a lamp, candle, signage, etc. must motivate the light. |
| **Camera type** | Auto, Modern, 35mm Film, 8mm Film, DV Camcorder | Base capture character. This is a look control, not a guarantee of a particular physical camera body. |
| **Lens** | Auto, Clean Sharp, Anamorphic, Vintage Anamorphic, Warm Vintage, Halation Vintage | Optical character. The official page enumerates Auto plus five actual lens looks. |
| **Aperture** | Auto, f/1.4 Wide Open, f/4 Moderate, f/11 Deep Focus | Depth-of-field intent. Use f/11 where environmental continuity matters; use f/1.4 only where loss of background detail is desired. |
| **Camera movement** | 30+ presets; documented examples include POV, Robot Arm, Pan Left, Helicopter Shot, tracking and pedestal-down | A camera path. Pick a single path appropriate to the beat; never also in the prompt (no double control, SKILL Render Slate `Settings`); a timing the preset cannot carry goes in the prompt and the preset stays Auto. |
| **References** | Up to 50 reference slots in one generation (the 4.0 guide's wording is "50 image references"; it does not enumerate classes). With **Seedance 2.5** selected, plan by ByteDance's official class split — 30 image + 10 video + 10 audio, incl. `@Clay Render` and `@Audio` (SKILL.md rule 5, video-prompting ch. 14b) — 🟡 whether the Cinema Studio upload widget exposes the video/audio slots is not yet receipted; confirm on the live subform and record it in the version ledger. Other models: read the active upload hint. | Attach references for identity, product shape, location, composition, style, motion and voice. Name/organize them in Elements where they recur. |

records.title: The browser surfaces a user can use
records.text:
| Surface | What it is for | Actual UI behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Model Gallery / model page** | Find a provider/model or operation | Each model page provides its own Playground and API documentation, pricing, average latency, and copyable examples. |
| **Playground** | Validate one specific model and reproduce the exact request | Fill its auto-generated form, click **Run**, see result(s), change fields and run again. The result retains generated code in Python, JavaScript, and cURL for that exact request. |
| **Sandbox** | Compare alternatives before committing | Run matching input/prompt across multiple models side-by-side; see estimated cost before submitting; search prior generations by text, image similarity, or dominant colour; share a preview link. It does **not** generate integration code. |
| **Dashboard** | Developer/account operations | Manage apps, API keys, billing, monitoring/analytics, requests, errors, and deployments. This is not the creative editing surface. |
| **Free browser tools** | Single-file utility jobs | Some background/remove/upscale/extend/resize tools run in-browser. Video-generation entries direct to Playground, require sign-in, and bill compute per second. |

records.title: What the Playground actually exposes
records.text:
| Schema pattern / metadata | Browser control rendered by Playground |
|---|---|
| `prompt` or `*_prompt` | Multi-line text area |
| `bool` | Toggle |
| bounded integer/float | Slider plus number input |
| `seed` | Number input plus randomize button |
| enum / literal | Dropdown |
| `*_image_url` / image field | Drag-drop, paste, or URL image upload and preview |
| `*_video_url` / video field | Video upload and preview |
| `*_audio_url` / audio field | Audio upload/player and microphone recording |
| `*_mask_image_url` / `*_mask_url` | Image input with built-in mask painter linked to the image field |
| `face_image_url` | Camera capture plus image upload |
| `camera_control` metadata | Visual movement selector with movement type/value |

records.title: API workflow an implementation agent may propose
records.text:
| Need | fal call pattern | Important boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Quick local prototype / fast request | `run()` | Direct call, no queue/retry/polling. |
| “Synchronous” developer convenience | `subscribe()` | Uses the queue but waits and handles polling. |
| Production parallel/batch work | `submit()` then status/result or webhook | Recommended route for control and reliability; it returns immediately. |
| Progressive updates | `stream()` | Only where endpoint supports it. |
| Very-low-latency interaction | `realtime()` | Persistent WebSocket, only for explicit real-time endpoints. |

records.title: Surface selection: the first decision
records.text:
| Surface | Use when | What an agent must not assume |
|---|---|---|
| **Tool Mode** | A single image/video generation or a named model’s direct settings | That an App’s convenience control will appear here. |
| **Apps** | A known operation such as keyframes, character swap, product video, relight, remove, or upscale | That Runway's first-party Apps are API-accessible — they are not; only a Workflow published as a custom App/endpoint is (see 'Agent and Workflows'). |
| **Agent** | A conversational multi-asset/multi-shot task, planning, scripts, moodboards, an assembled cut, or a guided iteration | That it should act without an outline/review. The user should review its plan before credit-spending. |
| **Workflows** | A reusable, explicit node graph/automation, including custom Apps | That it is an ordinary NLE timeline. It is a graph of model/utility nodes. |
| **Timeline Studio** | Trimming and arranging clips into a shorter cut | That it replaces an advanced local editor for a feature/complex finishing job. |

| **Studio / project** | Product image, image-generation model, scene prompt, selected image/output and downstream ad tools. Arcads auto-detects the uploaded product in its getting-started flow. | The product asset is the campaign anchor. Use it before asking a model to invent packaging, logo, or product details. |
| **Mark Agent** | Product site/assets, brand and audience information, competitor or winning-ad references, then a campaign request. | A conversational campaign-production route: Mark proposes angles/hooks/scripts, selects actors/scenes and produces an assembled UGC ad. It is not a reason to skip approval of factual claims, brand voice, product depiction, or the final ad. |
| **Workflows** | Explicit input/model/tool nodes, connected assets/prompts/actors, then Run. | A reusable batch pipeline. Treat each node’s visible input/output ports as canonical; do not assume that a Studio or Mark control exists as a node, or vice versa. |

records.title: Arcads: which form owns which user choice
records.text:
| User objective | Correct current route and verified direct choices | Do not transfer it to |
|---|---|---|
| Create product/lifestyle stills | **New Project → product upload → image generation**: product image, scene prompt, selected image model; the current flow also offers Prompt Builder and downstream changes to colours/background/elements. | Talking Actor, B-roll, or a generic Seedance/FLUX request without first checking the active model form. |
| Make a person deliver a UGC script | **Talking Actor**: choose a character from the generated image, choose a library voice or clone a voice, add script, optionally let Arcads add emotions, and preview audio before full video. | Animated Actor movement or a generic video model. The actor/script/voice/emotion form is its own surface. |
| Give the actor body/action movement | **Animated Actors**: select the visible movement model (current examples: Clean, Dance, Work), then its duration/aspect-ratio fields; after generation, voice/captions can be swapped. | Talking Actor speech settings, B-roll camera generation, or Cinema Studio camera controls. |
| Produce a product cutaway | **B-roll**: start from a product image, describe the shot, select the active B-roll model, then use that form’s short-clip/batch controls. The current guide gives Seedance 2.0 only as an example, not as a platform default. | Actor/voice/emotion options or a claim that every Arcads model exposes the same controls. |
| Localize an approved ad | **Translate**: choose target language and accent; Arcads describes automatic lip-motion matching. Review the language, claims and lip-sync result per locale. | A new Talking Actor or a text-only translation that is assumed to edit the old video automatically. |
| Generate many creative tests | **Workflow**: choose nodes, connect them, run the pipeline; current examples reuse a product image, script and character avatars across actors/languages. | A promise that an ad Agent/Studio generation will automatically preserve every node-level parameter. |

records.title: What to choose for the actual user request
records.text:
| User needs | Best first route | Why | Do not promise |
|---|---|---|---|
| Test the same source/prompt against several models, compare cost, then integrate in code | **fal Sandbox → specific Playground → API** | This is fal’s purpose-built comparison/reproducibility flow. | A shared set of model controls or a video-edit timeline. |
| Create or precisely revise a still in a conversational workspace | **ChatGPT native — ChatGPT Images 2.5 (`gpt-image-2.5` family — model choice: 'ChatGPT native image generation')** | It supports prompt-led reference use and iterative follow-up edits in one chat. | A native video render, external provider workspace, or API-only output controls. |
| Generate a provider image/video without leaving an MCP-capable chat/agent | **Named provider MCP**, after provider sign-in, workspace and credits are verified | Route choice: the route table in §0 'Mandatory route declaration'. | Web-UI parity, or an unexposed feature such as OpenArt Smart Shot (account boundary: 'Mandatory route declaration'). |
| Direct a cinematic shot with direct film-grammar settings, shared cast/assets, and a project context | **Higgsfield Cinema Studio 4.0** | Genre/era/tempo/light/camera/lens/aperture/Emotion Wheel are native UI controls — 🟡 whether they bite on Seedance 2.5 is settled per project by the §1 A/B ('Do the controls bite?'). | Output above the §1 verified 30 s / 1080p until the active dropdown confirms it. |
| Generate a controlled still and animate it with one current Runway model | **Runway Tool Mode: Gen-4 Image → Use → Gen-4.5 I2V** | The output handoff and reference process are documented. | Gen-4.5 start/end frames, video editing, or arbitrary external reference modes. |
| Replace/re-light/restyle/remove something in a short source video | **Runway Edit Studio** or the matching **OpenArt Video** edit tool | Both expose dedicated edit routes; use source constraints to choose. | That an arbitrary long/high-FPS/multi-cut clip will upload successfully. |
| Animate a character’s actual performance from an actor/driving clip | **Runway Act-Two** | It explicitly maps driving performance to character image/video and has gesture rules. | A full-body, multi-character, cut-heavy performance transfer without testing. |
| Make a multi-shot scene without hand-assembling every shot | **OpenArt Smart Shot** or **Runway Multi-Shot App** | Both are explicitly structured multi-shot modes; OpenArt shows a Shot Plan, Runway states up to five shots. | A conventional editable timeline from either generator. |
| Take a concept to an AI-assembled story/campaign/short video by conversation | **OpenArt Director** or **Runway Agent** | Both are chat-based planning/production surfaces, with different asset/timeline approaches. | Autonomous final approval or guaranteed cross-scene continuity. |
| Produce testable UGC/ad variations from product assets, actors, scripts and locales | **Arcads Studio → Talking/Animated Actor or B-roll → Workflow**; use **Mark** where a campaign-level conversational route is wanted | Its asset, actor, localization and batch surfaces are designed for creative testing. | Cinema-Studio film controls, generic model parity, unreviewed advertising claims, or automatic publication. |
| Preserve a recurring person/location/brand in OpenArt | **Character / World / Brand Kit** then the selected shot tool | This uses the suite’s persistent asset model. | Exact text/logo rendering or a model’s undocumented reference support. |
| Plan script → shots → storyboard → take/cut table in one shared planning document before any generation (storyboard-first model, workflows W10) | **FilmFlow Pro** (`FILMFLOW-WEB@2026-09-07`) if its frames stay look-free and it exports the production-pipeline ch. 2 schema; otherwise a Markdown shot board + grey sketches | Script, shot list and storyboard frames are one linked document with an animatic; the take/cut table and camera setup system are the skill's own additions on top. | AI renderings or an export/API — not on its public pages on the check date; any generation at all. |
| Need geometry-consistent location views | **OpenArt World → captured keyframes**; otherwise external 3D/blockout | World is a navigable persistent scene and captured output can seed video. | Current export to mesh/splats; it is not shipped in the cited source. |

records.title: Continuity strategy by platform
records.text:
| Platform | Agent-safe continuity mechanism |
|---|---|
| Higgsfield | Create/reuse Elements and Soul/AI Cast assets inside one project; add relevant references; use one project brief and shot folders. |
| fal.ai | Host/preserve canonical assets yourself and pass the URLs/files the selected endpoint accepts. The API result is a response with media URLs, not a film bible. |
| Runway | Create neutral character/environment plates; tag up to three reusable Gen-4 image References; store in Assets; animate approved stills. |
| OpenArt | Save Character, World, Brand Kit, and Media assets; attach them in the selected tool or tag them in Director. |
| Arcads | Retain the approved product asset, actor/voice choice, script, locale and winning creative structure; make all of them explicit Workflow inputs when scaling. |
| ChatGPT native | Keep the approved image and its reference/prompt context in the conversation while iterating; deliberately download/attach the final still when another provider must use it. |

records.title: 2. Red/yellow list (avoid or mitigate)
records.text:
| Element | Failure | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **In-frame text — unified rule** | Text, logos, subtitles, formulas render as scribble or drift between frames | Default: ALL exact on-screen text goes to post-compositing (officially confirmed [BD-off]). Three documented exceptions: (a) **static short text locked via master plate** — content frozen in the reference image + prompt lock "exactly this one line, frozen and identical in every frame" (production-proven, platforms-models ch. 13b); (b) 🟡 MiniMax H3 has an official quoted-text channel (visible text in double quotes, verbatim, untranslated [MM-off]) and renders UI/text comparatively stably — syntax documented, quality practitioner-rated: test before relying. Dynamic/changing text stays red everywhere. 🟡 Exception (c) — DESIGNED typography as the product: Higgsfield Marketing Studio's motion-design presets (launch video, hypermotion product ad, 2D and editorial explainer, 3D real-estate flythrough with pricing overlays) render text overlays, numbers and animated charts as the generation's subject, and the vendor shows them "locked, not melting" including minutes of editorial text [H-off, P68 — vendor demo, not frame-checked here]; a different generation class from a video model rendering incidental text. Every word and number is still checked against the script before delivery, and the rule for generative FILM shots is unchanged. 🟡 Exception (a) confirmed on 2.5 by [P54]: a one-word character-intro title generated INTO the Seedream 5.0 Pro still and carried by Seedance 2.5 over 20 s with a spelling lock in the prompt ("the name is Dan — exactly D-A-N, not Dann, not Dane") — single short static word, plate-locked; still the exception. |
| Crowds | Clone extras, melting faces in distance | Multi-variant sheet (production-pipeline ch. 3) with extras as silhouette-distinct CLASSES ("heavy brute" / "light scout") — classes, not outfit variants, kill the clone read; crowds to mid/background; small faces stay unreliable even at high res; fog capped as a visible relation ("everything past the third rank dissolves into fog" — never a distance in metres, SKILL rule 7) hides background glitches at army scale (less needed at 4K, still works) [H-off, P25]; formations (66 dancers in rings around a singer) hold across cuts when positions and facing come from blockout boxes and only the movement is prompted [H-off, P66]; a cast of ten distinct extras saved as one element stops per-shot face regeneration [H-off, P69] |
| Hands + fine object manipulation | Finger errors, object morphing | Close-ups only as short single-action beats, cut away before the fine work; the handling invariant is written once as a lock sentence — inside the beat on the Caption Spine (ch. 12h), as a POSITIVE LOCKS line in the block structure ("ALWAYS by the handle") — there is no separate CRITICAL block |
| Vehicles/wheels/mechanics | Wrong rotation, illogical mechanics | See rescue paths below |
| Long continuous camera moves | Collapse after several moves (proven in 2.5 too) | One move per shot; cuts instead of tours |
| Instrument fingering, precise sports technique | Approximate only | Frame around it; cutaways |
| Physics as hero (glass shattering exactly, complex fluid pours) | Plausible-but-wrong | Describe end state; hide peak behind cut |
| Tiny hero object carrying the beat (a key, a pill, a seed in a hand) | Object morphs, vanishes or changes size between frames; detail vs. size contradiction (ch. 24b) | Cut to an insert as its own short shot at close scale; carry the beat by the character's reaction; object as a prop sheet (production-pipeline ch. 4) |
| Dark, figure-less macro (no scale anchor, no figure, low light) | No scale read, no material read — the model fills with generic texture or invents a subject | Add a scale anchor or a figure (SKILL rule 9 on stylized projects), lift a motivated practical, or replace by a still + ellipsis |
| Continuous approach over distance (a walk/drive/flight that must close the gap on camera) | Scale collapses on the way (same class as wide-shot scale, above); the approach stalls or teleports | Two shots: departure state, arrival state — the distance is an ellipsis (manual cut); never one continuous take |
| Cut back onto the same emissive object (lamp, screen, fire) whose state must match frame-exactly | Brightness, colour temperature and shape differ between takes; the object appears "re-lit" | One state per state sheet (production-pipeline ch. 4); the second view inside the same take, or the object kept in one setup (W10 anchor composition); otherwise accept a grade-side match (post-audio-legal ch. 17) |
| **Wide shots** (stylized 3D; photoreal crowd scale too) | Scale and distance break at wide range; a flat camera path at constant height/speed leaves characters as dots (vendor-confirmed on Higgsfield's own short and its Hell Grind rebuild) | Open the take on a close/medium of the character and transition into the wide inside the same generation; positions locked by the previs/clay render, not by the wide (pixar-look §10) |
| Faces that must stay blank (silent passengers, listeners with no beat) | Model animates them anyway — micro-expressions, drift | Hide by design with a motivated occlusion: reflective glass, backlight silhouette, hat brim, distance — copy-ready GLASS block in video-prompting 12e |
| **Mirror/reflection beats** where a reflected face or pose must match the subject frame-exactly | Reflected face/pose diverges from the subject; reflection doubled, missing, or lagging a beat behind | 🟡 (derivation, not yet [PP]-tested) Reflections as texture/light — glass, water, wet street, chrome — stay GREEN on Seedance 2.5 (§1). For a story mirror beat: Seedance 2.5 only, static camera, ONE readable face in frame — either the reflection alone (subject from behind / over the shoulder) or the subject alone with the mirror as shape (film-craft §2 frame-in-frame); never subject and reflection both readable; otherwise split subject and reflection across a cut. 🟢 Blockout rescue [H-off, P66]: a camera passing THROUGH a mirror held in one 15-s continuous take when the set was blocked as a mirrored twin with both characters moving in sync and the mirror as an opening (production-pipeline ch. 8 protocol b). |

records.title: 4. Format matrix (what each look forgives)
records.text:
| Format | Fit | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Pixar/stylized 3D** | **Excellent — safest "cinema look"** | Stylization absorbs physics/texture errors; audiences expect no real physics. Look definition and evidence: pixar-look.md |
| High-action anime | Excellent | Speed lines/held poses mask model weaknesses |
| UGC/found footage | Excellent | Degradation hides artifacts |
| Photoreal drama, static dialogue | Good with discipline | Reverse plates + framing recycling mandatory |
| Flat 2D/limited animation | Hard | Punishes every wobble; simple motion only (style-control §5b) |
| Photoreal action with hero physics | Hardest | Plan rescue cuts per risk shot |
